heading here may mark its own section historical.

the project, and nothing may be acted on without re-verifying it live against the source
of truth first. Everything here has already been superseded, pruned, or archived out of a

## CS-1281

### Filed 2026-10-08 by CS-1266's builder

The shipped docs carry `mCanChangePotential` - of 68 registry buildings, 24 True, 38 False, and
6 omit it - but `clockspeed/data/registry.py` does not read it, so the balance's elided-clock
count includes classes that cannot be clocked: up to 46 of 128 elided machines per world are
non-clockable classes. The `BACKLOG.md` Session 124 elided-count line was folded into CS-1266's
slice, but with no registry field to read it was not done there.

### Measured 2026-10-09 by CS-1281's builder

One sibling of the same root cause sits outside the slice and is NOT changed by it:
`clockspeed/audit/flow.py::_clock_of` counts an untagged flowing machine elided with no
registry input at all, so `WorldFlow.elided_clock_count` would still count a non-clockable
class that runs a recipe. Whether any such class runs a recipe was not measured. The
CS-1265 agreement arm, `tests/audit/test_flow.py::test_the_flow_and_the_balance_classify_every_clock_alike`,
stays green only because its synthetic buildings leave `clockable` None.

### Acceptance

the registry reads the field, and an unknown or absent value stays a named unknown, never defaulted; the balance's elided count excludes a class that cannot be clocked; an arm with a synthetic non-clockable class reddens when it is counted elided; the `BACKLOG.md` Session 124 elided-count line is relocated as discharged

From section 5, Self-adjudicating:

A tree that edits itself mid-verdict makes the ruling a statement about no state at all,
and any finding repaired while the adjudicator writes is one it cannot see it discharged.
Measured in session 45: the tree moved under an adjudicator four times, and three
whole-suite runs were spent proving that a run straddling an edit says nothing.

From section 2.3, Output constraints:

The operator watches several project sessions side by side, so prose in the main transcript
costs tokens on both ends AND buries the thing being decided. A quiet session is one where
the tool-call labels carry the narration.

## CS-1266

### Filed 2026-10-04 by CS-500's S4 adversary pass

`power.draw_incomplete` scopes "complete" to the audit's considered population, but the clocked
draw can report complete while omitting a built power consumer that has no clock, no recipe and no
producing tag. Nothing cross-checks the considered population against what is actually built.

### Acceptance

the audit publishes, like for like, the count of built power consumers and the count its clocked draw considered, and a consumer the draw omits is named; an arm with a synthetic world holding such a consumer reddens when the omission goes unnamed

## CS-1278

### Filed 2026-10-08 by CS-1265's adversary pass

`clockspeed/audit/flow.py` prices a machine's output by its clock alone, but a production boost
also multiplies output. Once CS-1264 lands, the balance names a boosted machine a
boost-unmodeled gap while the flow audit flows it - at the elided default when it carries no
clock tag - so two audits over one world disagree about one machine, the CS-1265 defect one
axis over. Waits on CS-1264.

### Acceptance

a machine carrying a production-boost tag, decoded or not (CS-1264's `MachineState.production_boost_tagged`), is a named flow gap, never flowed at its clock alone, and is excluded from the elided count; the both-audits arm, `tests/audit/test_flow.py::test_the_flow_and_the_balance_classify_every_clock_alike`, gains a boosted row and still asserts the two audits classify every machine alike; an arm reddens when the flow ignores the boost

## CS-1264

### Filed 2026-10-04 by CS-1263's adversary pass

`clockspeed/audit/balance.py::clocked_draw_of` prices an elided or tagged machine by its clock
alone and never checks a production boost, so the balance reason line is false for a boosted
machine. The 40-save library carries no boost tag, so no real save exercises it yet; the fix must
not invent a boost reading, it must refuse or name what it cannot read.

### Acceptance

a machine carrying a production-boost tag is either priced by the boosted power law or published as a named gap, never priced as unboosted; an arm with a synthetic boosted machine reddens when the boost is ignored; the elided-default count excludes a boosted machine

### Filed 2026-10-08 by the session 131 CS-G03 walk

The CS-G03 clean-machine re-walk ran at `ed0b03f` in a fresh Windows Sandbox, walked by a
context-free agent. It reached the README first result; `scripts/verify_env.py` exited 0; the
hooks were armed - a staged violation was refused with HEAD unchanged, and a control commit was
committed. But the full suite, run as the docs then stated, was RED: 14383 passed, 302 skipped,
24 failed, 17 errors. 35 of the 41 needed Git for Windows' `usr\bin` on PATH (`openssl`,
`bash`), which no doc required for the suite; the other 6, in
`tests/ops/test_inbox_responder.py`, built paths over MAX_PATH with Windows long paths off, the
Windows default. The walk also found six README defects: D1, no clone command; D2, the Python
PATH option; D3, PowerShell venv activation; D4, the `curl` alias in PowerShell; D5, a stale
Status section; D6, the suite's prerequisites - plus no git identity step in any newcomer doc.

The repairs landed in the CS-1279 commit "walk repairs: short responder paths, README,
OPERATIONS" (`457d2b9`): D2 to D6 in `README.md`; the suite's `usr\bin` need and the git
identity step in `docs/OPERATIONS.md`; short planted paths in
`tests/ops/test_inbox_responder.py`, graded by
`tests/ops/test_inbox_responder.py::test_every_planted_note_fits_max_path_on_a_default_machine`.
D1 is deferred to the CS-700 flip, when the public address exists. A repair is not a pass: walk
1 stands FAILED, and this item closes only on the second walk its acceptance names.

### Acceptance

a second walk by a different context-free agent in a fresh Windows Sandbox with long paths off, at a tip at or after the CS-1279 repair commit, follows `README.md` and the `docs/OPERATIONS.md` bootstrap as written and records `scripts/verify_env.py` exit 0, the hook violation refused with HEAD unchanged plus a committed control, and the full suite run as documented with 0 failed and 0 errors; an adjudicator that did not walk grades the log. Walk logs live outside the repo.

## CS-1265

### Filed 2026-10-04 by CS-1263's adversary pass

`clockspeed/audit/flow.py` returns `GAP_FLOW_CLOCK_UNREAD` for a machine with no clock tag, which
is most of the library, while `clockspeed/audit/balance.py` prices the same machine at the elided
default under CS-1263's ruling. Two audits over one world disagree about one fact. The CS-1263
decision governs: an untagged machine on a cleanly read payload is at the class default unless a
measured save shows otherwise.

### Acceptance

the flow audit reads the same `overclock_elided` mark the balance reads and treats an elided machine as at the class default, counted, while a refused or unread clock stays a named gap; one arm drives both audits over one synthetic world and asserts they classify every machine's clock the same way

adds; clause (b) is retired; the vendoring the "Here:" paragraph deferred landed with
CS-1272; the rule-4 mechanism is owned by `CONVENTIONS.md` section 10. The tooling-map
rows CS-1272 moved are not here - they are live, in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` section 6.

```text
notification; (b) section 2.3.1 is kit v7 item 13 as this tree applies it, and governs
over the embedded block's item 3 "no inline checklists" until the v7 block is re-embedded; (c) FLEET item 10 has one stated
```

```text
**THE CHECKLIST IS THE STATUS FORMAT, NOT PROSE - kit v7 item 13 (MAIN, 2026-10-05).**
At session start, planned from the hand-off and the roadmap before any work, print
`Session <n> checklist`, then one line per task in execution order:
`<box> <ID>: <imperative task, one line> (<state>, ~ETA)` - the parenthesis only while the
task runs. `<box>` is U+2610; tracked files name it by that text, never the glyph (section
3 rule 4). The LAST line is `<box> /done`. At most ONE trailing sentence, only when an
ordering constraint matters. No summary, review or history.

After every FOUR OR MORE completed tasks, print ONLY the remaining tasks plus new ones,
marked `+` before the ID - never a completed one. A status request gets the same
remaining-only list. When no task remains, `/done` runs UNPROMPTED and its chat output
stays one line. Section 6.1 owns adjudicate-do-not-ask and commit-and-push; keep the
remaining context in mind when planning `/done`.

**Here:** n is the `SESSION: <n>` line of `CS-NEXT-SESSION.txt`; `/done` writes n+1
(`.claude/commands/done.md`), and the session-start hand-off read prints the block. The
headless paths (`ops/loop/inbox_responder.py`, `ops/loop/queue_loop.py`) print nothing
yet: they, the kit vendoring and the block re-embed land in one commit straight after
CS-700 S12a - `docs/LEDGER.md`, FLEET-KIT v7 decision C.
```

```text
Rule 4 has a mechanism, not just a preference behind it: Windows PowerShell 5.1
ANSI-decodes a `.ps1` with no BOM, and a UTF-8 em-dash inside a double-quoted string
becomes a character the tokenizer treats as a string terminator. One incident made it
permanent. Use a spaced hyphen ` - ` for a clause break.
```

## CS-1269

### Filed 2026-10-04 by CS-500's close

`/api/advice/<id>/state` is where a card is accepted, dismissed, snoozed or pinned, so it
writes the per-world ledger through `clockspeed/advisor/ledger.py::Ledger.set_state` and
`snooze`. The ledger is ready, but the route stays 501 because the listener is not ready for a
write. `clockspeed/surface/server.py` checks no `Origin`, no `Sec-Fetch-Site` and no
custom header, and the handler contract passes query parameters only. A cross-site page in
the operator's own browser could therefore post a form to the loopback port and dismiss or
snooze cards without being seen. CS-1261 hardens the read side. This item is the write side,
and it lands after or together with the refusal it needs.

Before CS-500 closed, this route blamed CS-500. It now blames this item through
`clockspeed/surface/api/pending.py::BLOCKERS`.

### Acceptance

red first: a POST to `/api/advice/<id>/state` that carries no same-origin proof, such as a required custom request header that a cross-site form cannot send, is refused and the ledger file is unchanged byte for byte; a POST that carries the proof records `accepted`, `dismissed`, `pinned` or a `snoozed` state with a future `until` for a card the current advice lists, read back from disk; an unknown card or state kind is 400 and reflects nothing; a GET stays 405; `pending.BLOCKERS` and `contract.OPEN_BLOCKERS` lose CS-1269

## CS-1268

### Filed 2026-10-04 by CS-500's close

`BOOTSTRAP.md` section 5.2 requires that `completed` is set automatically when the world state
satisfies the advice, and calls that transition worth surfacing. It is never set:
`clockspeed/advisor/ledger.py` offers no listing of a world's recorded cards, so
`clockspeed/advisor/advise.py::advise` sees only the cards that fire now and cannot detect a
recorded card that has vanished; and `advise` writes neither store by design
(`tests/advisor/test_advise.py::test_advise_never_writes_either_store`), so the transition
needs a stated write path. A Phase 5 product item, not tooling.

`BOOTSTRAP.md` does NOT state what a completed card does when its rule fires again. Ruled here
on the section's own wording - `completed` means the world satisfies the advice, so a firing
rule means it no longer does: a completed card that fires again is surfaced as `new`, and a
card the player set `dismissed`, `snoozed` or `pinned` keeps that state and is never marked
`completed` over it. Recorded with this filing; an adjudicator may overrule it before build.

### Acceptance

red first: a synthetic world where a card is recorded `accepted` or `new` and shown, then a reload in which its rule stops firing, leaves that card `completed` in the per-world ledger, read back from disk, and the transition is surfaced in the result; the ledger can list one world's recorded cards; a `completed` card whose rule fires again is surfaced as `new`; a `dismissed`, `snoozed` or `pinned` card whose rule stops firing keeps its state; two runs over the same inputs give the same states

## CS-1059

### Filed 2026-09-14

**THE PANEL IS A COMPARISON AND ONLY ONE SIDE EXISTS.** CS-1045 delivered the exact world
DRAW as a Fraction sum over built counts. Generated power has no `Building` field and no
extractor anywhere, so `production_available` is published False with a warning rather than
a zero. The headline the item promised - production versus consumption - currently has one
operand.

**THE REFUSAL TO PUBLISH A ZERO IS THE PRECEDENT TO COPY.** `DrawGap` declares no megawatts
field at all, so an unmodeled draw CANNOT be represented as zero; the impossibility is
structural and is graded off the dataclass's own fields. Generated power must be built the
same way. A zero that means "not modelled" is a number that looks like a measurement, which
is non-negotiable 7.

**THE FLAG IS PART OF THE ACCEPTANCE, NOT PLUMBING.** `production_available` must become True
only when a production figure was actually computed, and an arm must redden if it is written
as a literal. This is the same defect CS-1058 carries for the topology flags, and both were
created by the same habit of declaring an absence with a constant.

### Filed 2026-10-04 by a builder's read-only measurement

**THE DATA EXISTS; ONLY THE EXTRACTOR IS MISSING.** A read-only probe of the shipped docs
file found a scalar `mPowerProduction` on every class of the `FGBuildableGeneratorFuel` and
`FGBuildableGeneratorNuclear` groups. "No extractor anywhere" was true of the code and is
not a negative about the game: generated power IS derivable from the sanctioned source.

**THE GEOTHERMAL TRAP IS THE VARIABLE-DRAW TRAP AGAIN.** The `FGBuildableGeneratorGeoThermal`
class declares `mPowerProduction` as `'0.000000'` and carries its real output on
`mVariablePowerProductionConstant`, `mVariablePowerProductionFactor` and a cycle length
and offset - the same shape `clockspeed/data/registry.py` already documents for the
variable-power consumers. Reading the scalar alone publishes a confident zero. Until the
cycle is modelled exactly, that class must land as a NAMED gap. Every generator also
declares `mPowerConsumption` as `'0.000000'`, so the existing draw partition must not
start counting a generator as a zero-draw consumer when the extractor lands.

**SEAM - THE WORK IS IN THREE LAYERS NO `save/` OR `solve/` SLICE OWNS.** The extractor
belongs in `clockspeed/data/registry.py`, the sum and the computed flag in
`clockspeed/audit/balance.py`, and the graded arm module under `tests/audit/`. The
write-list was widened to those three and the work landed there.

**WHAT REMAINS AT THE WIRING SITE.** `balance_of` computes production only when a
caller passes the registry's generator namespace, so the flag stays False on every
surface until `clockspeed/advisor/advise.py` passes it - a one-argument change in a
layer this slice did not own. The figure is a NAMEPLATE capacity at the reference
clock: a generator's clock law and fuel state are unmeasured, so it is never live
output. An adversary found the placement allowlist in `clockspeed/audit/placement.py`
dropped the fuel, nuclear and geothermal generators, so the capacity read complete
without them; they are admitted now, and an arm runs the repro through `placement_of`.
A generator class a FUTURE build adds to the registry but not to that allowlist would
still be dropped there - the residual is recorded, not closed.

### Acceptance

a new arm module under `tests/audit/` asserts generated power is the exact Fraction sum over built generators, that a generator class the registry does not model contributes a NAMED gap rather than a zero exactly as `DrawGap` already refuses to carry one, and that the balance's own `production_available` flag becomes True only when a production figure was actually computed - reddening if it is written as a literal

### Full headline

the power panel is production versus consumption and only consumption exists: CS-1045 delivered the exact world draw but found NO `Building` field and no extractor for generated power anywhere, so it publishes `production_available` False with a warning rather than a zero, and the headline comparison the item promised has one side

## CS-1267 - item section, CLOSED and relocated from `docs/item_notes/phase7.md` 2026-10-04

## CS-1267

### Filed 2026-10-04 by the CS-700 pre-S7a batch run

`tools/flip_checks.py::clone_at` makes a local `git clone --no-checkout`, which hard-links the
source's object files, including `.git/objects/info/commit-graph`. A concurrent git process holds
that file open, so removing the run's scratch directory fails and the whole run exits 1 even when
every check passed - measured at S1 on the pre-S7a batch: 0 of 9 checks failed, exit 1 from
cleanup alone. It blocks a clean S1 and S8 exit, so it blocks CS-700. A leftover scratch directory
`.git/flip-checks/run-jwsav2xk` from that run is removed once nothing holds it. The fix clones with
`--no-hardlinks`; it must not swallow a cleanup failure to get exit 0.

### Acceptance

the flip-checks clone shares no hard-linked object file with the source repository; an arm asserts the clone command carries `--no-hardlinks` (or that no object file of the clone shares an inode with the source); a run whose checks all pass exits 0 while another git process holds the source's commit-graph open; a genuine cleanup failure still fails the run and names the path

### MEASURED 2026-10-04, the fix on its slice branch, not yet closed

`clone_at` now passes `--no-hardlinks`, and a scratch tree that will not go is named relative to
the repository in the run's output, never as an absolute path. The hold that blocks cleanup is a
MAPPING, as git holds it: a plain open handle on the commit-graph does not stop the clone's link
from being unlinked, so an arm that holds it with `open()` alone passes against the defect. The
four arms in `tests/test_flip_checks.py`, each observed red before the fix:
`test_the_clone_command_carries_no_hardlinks`,
`test_no_clone_object_file_shares_an_inode_with_the_source`,
`test_a_passing_run_exits_zero_while_the_commit_graph_is_held` (mmap hold, with a Windows control
that the hold blocks unlinking a second name) and
`test_a_genuine_cleanup_failure_fails_the_run_and_names_the_path`. Closing needs the `ROADMAP.md`
line removed and a `docs/LEDGER.md` entry, plus removal of the leftover `run-jwsav2xk` scratch
directory under the primary checkout's git directory.

## CS-1263

### Filed 2026-10-04 by CS-1235's round trip

`clockspeed/audit/balance.py::draw_of` prices each built class at its declared reference
draw times the BUILT count and never reads a clock, while the solver prices a step at its
fractional machine count. Over a materialised plan the audit exceeds the solver by exactly
`sum(draw * (ceil(m) - m))` - 24 against 20 MW on the C1 chain at 50 per minute - and the two
agree only on all-integral plans. Pinned, not repaired, at
`tests/audit/test_round_trip.py`. NEITHER FIGURE IS PHYSICAL: an underclocked machine draws
`draw * clock ** exponent`, which `clockspeed/solve/power.py::draw_at_clock` reports as
deferred, so the honest answer is a bounded interval, which is CS-1064's territory. Do not
close this by making the audit read fractional machines - a world has whole machines.

### Acceptance

the audit's draw reads each machine's clock and publishes the clock-scaled draw as an exact value where the power law yields one and as a named bound where it does not, and the round-trip power arm compares like with like: the pinned divergence test is replaced by an equality or bound check that reddens when the clock is ignored

### Evidence measured 2026-10-04

EVIDENCED, not closed here. The clock-scaled draw is `clockspeed/audit/balance.py::clocked_draw_of`, carried as `WorldBalance.clocked_draw`: exact at the reference clock, at a whole exponent and at a zero clock (`tests/audit/test_balance.py::test_the_reference_clock_is_exact_under_any_exponent`, `tests/audit/test_balance.py::test_a_whole_exponent_away_from_the_reference_clock_is_exact`, `tests/audit/test_balance.py::test_a_zero_clock_is_exact_zero_under_a_positive_exponent`); a named bound otherwise (`tests/audit/test_balance.py::test_a_fractional_exponent_is_a_named_bound_bracketing_the_law`, `tests/audit/test_balance.py::test_the_bracket_contains_the_physical_draw`); an unread clock a named gap, never one (`tests/audit/test_balance.py::test_an_unread_clock_is_a_named_gap_never_one`); an elided clock tag priced at the default and counted (`tests/audit/test_balance.py::test_an_elided_clock_is_priced_exactly_at_the_default_and_counted`). The pinned divergence test is replaced by `tests/audit/test_round_trip.py::test_audit_draw_upper_bound_equals_solver_figure_on_fractional_plans`, `tests/audit/test_round_trip.py::test_audit_draw_is_exact_and_equals_solver_figure_on_integral_plans` and `tests/audit/test_round_trip.py::test_the_clocked_draw_reddens_when_the_clock_is_ignored`.

## CS-1228

### Acceptance

live arm in `tests/test_sha_citation_gate.py` can judge it, and
`tests/test_full_history_checkouts.py` - red first against the shallow checkout - pins

The windows legs of `suite` and `clean-checkout-probe` complete inside their
`timeout-minutes`, whose value is stated beside it as a measured wall plus a stated
margin. Closed only by a tier2 run on the landed tip in which both legs of both jobs
conclude `success`, its measured windows walls recorded at close.

### Full headline

the nightly tier2 full suite is shallow-checked-out and its windows legs outrun a
30-minute cutoff, so the lane has not been green since 2026-09-24

### FILED 2026-10-03, measured from the tier2 run history by the main session

Every scheduled tier2 run 2026-09-25..2026-10-03 concluded `cancelled` or `failure`. Two
defects, independent of each other. FIRST, the `suite` checkout carried no `fetch-depth`,
so the CS-1222 live arm failed - by design, never skipping - on the shallow clone; the
ubuntu leg of run 37112434671 was red on exactly that one test, while the module's
docstring claims CI runs it only in tier1's full-history save shard. The probe job was
unaffected: it checks out with `fetch-depth: 0` and clones from that. SECOND, the windows
legs of `suite` and `clean-checkout-probe` were cancelled at the 30-minute cutoff on every
night, ended by the cutoff and not by a failing step: the last progress line of the
pytest step put it at 75 to 88 per cent after 29 minutes, a projected wall of 33.0 to 39.0
minutes (suite) and 28.5 to 38.8 (probe). Both legs already ran `-n auto`, so this is
suite growth, not lost parallelism: the last green windows suite passed 10456 tests on
2026-09-25, the 2026-10-03 ubuntu leg 12518 (one of them the shallow failure). The ubuntu
legs reached 28.6 minutes; on 2026-10-01 both jobs' ubuntu legs were cancelled at 99 and
97 per cent.

THE REPAIR, AND WHAT IT LEAVES OPEN. `fetch-depth: 0` on the `suite` checkout; both jobs
now run `--dist loadfile`, the scheduler tier1 and the pre-push hook already use; both
cutoffs raised 30 to 50, sized as the worst projected wall plus under a minute of job
overhead divided by the CS-1124 headroom fraction of 4/5. The loadfile gain on the
windows runner is unmeasured, so the ceiling does not count on it. The suite grew by over
a third in eleven days (9061 passed on 2026-09-22); at that rate the 4/5 headroom guard
reddens again within weeks, and the honest next step is sharding the tier2 suite the way tier1 is sharded,
which renames jobs and so needs `tools/tier2_durations.json` refreshed in the same
change. The `tests/test_sha_citation_gate.py` docstring sentence naming tier1's save
shard as the only CI home of the module is now false and wants correcting.

### MEASURED 2026-10-03 on the first tier2 run carrying the repair

Run 37125738113 at 87ea30c. Ubuntu legs: the shallow failure is gone; both reddened only
on a git auto-maintenance race in a `tests/test_freeze_witness.py` fixture, repaired in the
same batch. Windows suite: pytest reported 2799s (46m39s) under the 50-minute cutoff, one
failure (CS-1230). Windows probe: CANCELLED at the 50-minute cutoff at 99 per cent. So
`--dist loadfile` did not buy the windows margin, and a further raise is not the repair:
this item closes only once CS-1229 shards the suite and a tier2 run is green on both OSes.

**A THIRD AXIS, added 2026-08-22 (session 32) by the fourth CS-703 adversary. The
acceptance text names cleanup mode and commit path; `core.commentChar` is a third and the
matrix is wider than filed.** Measured: with `core.commentChar` remapped, a line led by the
ordinary comment character is NOT a comment to git, survives cleanup into the stored

Filed 2026-08-22 (session 31); the item stays OPEN in `ROADMAP.md`.

Filed 2026-08-22 (session 31) by the adjudicator of the widened CS-702 grant, which MEASURED the subject-cap escape that nothing else had named.

**THE ROOT FACT: cleanup runs AFTER the commit-msg hook.** On the editor path the hook sees the full
template while the stored message has it stripped, so every check in that hook PREDICTS the stored
bytes and never observes them. The pre-filter drops comment lines and truncates at the scissors
token unconditionally, so it models one mode out of five.

**MEASURED, with real commits and clean controls.** A 200-character comment line as the first line
becomes a 215-character STORED subject with the hook exiting 0 and HEAD moving. A comment line
carrying an em dash lands three bytes above 0x7E in the stored message. Both need only a comment
line - no scissors marker, no flags, no configuration.

**THE CLEANUP TABLE, measured.** `verbatim` and `whitespace` keep comments and keep everything below
the scissors marker. `strip` removes comments and KEEPS what is below the marker. `scissors`
truncates only on the editor path. `default` is `strip` when edited and `whitespace` when not.
Note the consequence: today's unconditional break is wrong on the ordinary editor path too.

**THE OBSERVABLE EXISTS.** Git sets `GIT_EDITOR` to the no-op colon in the hook environment exactly
when the editor was not used. `commit.cleanup` is readable too. What is NOT observable is an
explicit cleanup override combined with an editor, which is the admitted residual.

**WHY 78 GREEN TESTS COEXISTED WITH THREE FAIL-OPENS,** which is the transferable part: every arm
drove one commit path, and one arm ASSERTED THE ESCAPE AS INTENDED BEHAVIOUR. The defective mode
was simultaneously the only mode tested and the mode declared correct. Any suite for this item must
parameterize over cleanup mode by commit path, and must use GIT AS THE ORACLE FOR THE STORED BYTES
- read `git log -1` back from the landed commit and assert the gate blocked if and only if the
stored message violates - rather than asserting against its own model of what git will do.

The trailer half of the same defect is CS-702 and the routes no client-side hook can cover are
CS-704. This item owns the cleanup model, the ASCII escape and the subject-cap escape.

### Measured 2026-08-24 (session 38): the FOURTH leak, salvaged from an inherited worktree and re-derived

**SALVAGED, THEN RE-DERIVED RATHER THAN IMPORTED.** This was built in an inherited worktree
on 2026-08-22, never committed, and was the only record of it anywhere in the project. It was
re-measured from scratch on 2026-08-24 against git 2.53.0.windows.3 in a throwaway repository
before being written here, so what follows is a measurement and not a quotation.

**THE CLEANUP TABLE ABOVE IS INCOMPLETE IN ONE ROW.** `verbatim` additionally preserves
TRAILING WHITESPACE on every line. Under `whitespace`, `strip`, `default` and `scissors`, git
runs its trailing-whitespace pass BEFORE the commit-msg hook; under `verbatim` it does not run
at all. Measured with a first line of 70 characters followed by five spaces:

| cleanup mode | bytes the hook is handed | bytes the commit object stores |
|---|---|---|
| `verbatim` | 75 | 75 |
| `whitespace`, `strip`, `default`, `scissors` | 70 | 70 |

**THE FOURTH LEAK ITSELF.** A subject measured AFTER trimming reads 70 against a cap of 72 and
commits, while the object stores 75. The subject must be measured UNTRIMMED. This is a fourth
escape distinct from the three this item already owns, and it bites under `verbatim` and only
under `verbatim`.

**AND THE ORACLE THIS SECTION PRESCRIBES CANNOT SEE IT.** The paragraph above instructs any
acceptance suite to use git as the oracle by reading `git log -1` back from the landed commit.
MEASURED: `git log -1 --format=%s` renders 70 for the very commit whose object stores 75 - the
placeholder normalises the trailing run away. So the prescribed oracle is BLIND to exactly this
leak, and a suite built on it would stay green while the escape is live. Read the raw bytes
with `git cat-file commit HEAD` and split the header from the body instead. THIS WAS FOUND BY
FALLING INTO IT: the first probe run for this block used `%s`, reported 70 stored under
`verbatim`, and would have refuted a true claim. It is the standing "a probe can validate the
wrong channel" failure, landing on this item's own written instruction.

### Acceptance

a message whose STORED bytes carry a byte above 0x7E, or a stored subject over the cap, is BLOCKED whichever cleanup mode and commit path git actually uses, proven end to end across the mode-by-path matrix rather than on one path

**A THIRD HANG SHAPE, added 2026-08-22 (session 32) by the fourth CS-703 adversary.**
A wrapper of the form `exec python "$@" < /dev/null` answers BOTH probe halves exactly -
the token, then 97 - and then hangs `commit-msg` forever, measured at 124 under a 30 second
cap with HEAD unmoved. Root cause measured: under MSYS bash `/dev/null` maps to Windows
`NUL`, a CHARACTER DEVICE, so `isatty()` reports true, `python -` goes interactive, and the
3.14 REPL spins on an invalid handle. It is DISTINCT from the two shapes above - this
candidate spawns nothing and sets no environment variable - and it is further evidence that
the answer is a BOUND rather than an enumeration of causes.


Filed 2026-08-22 (session 32); the item stays OPEN in `ROADMAP.md`.

TWO SHAPES, both measured, one pre-existing and one introduced by CS-819's capture.

**Shape one, PRE-EXISTING in the old probe and unchanged by the repair.** `PYTHONINSPECT=1` makes the
candidate enter interactive mode after running the program, and it never returns. Measured at a
bounded six seconds returning 124 - **WITH stdin already redirected from `/dev/null`**, so closing
stdin does NOT close this. Neither the old probe nor the new one is timeout-bounded, and a hung hook
looks like frozen git rather than a refusal.

**Shape two, introduced by the CS-819 capture and disclosed in its grant.** Command substitution
waits for EOF on the pipe rather than for the child to exit, so a program that spawns a background
process holding stdout stalls the hook for that process's whole lifetime. Measured at 124 under a
bound. LATENT today: the program the hook delivers spawns nothing.

**The route, and its cost.** `timeout` exists at `/usr/bin/timeout` here and on a POSIX runner, but
adding it makes the hooks depend on a binary they currently do not need, and `CONVENTIONS.md` section
16 says such findings are version-specific. Whatever ships must FAIL CLOSED on a timeout - a probe
that times out and then proceeds is the CS-703 defect wearing a clock.

### Acceptance

a hook whose probe does not answer within a bounded time REFUSES rather than hanging, proven with PYTHONINSPECT=1 and a real commit asserting a non-zero exit inside the bound

`pre-commit` never checks ruff at all, and `tools/precommit_gate.py` treats a missing ruff as
LINT SKIPPED rather than blocking - so a resolved python without ruff silently degrades the
character-set gate's sibling checks rather than refusing.

### Acceptance

a hook whose resolved interpreter cannot import the tools that hook needs REFUSES, proven with an interpreter that is genuinely python and genuinely missing them

## CS-1018

### Acceptance

the 262.5s gap is attributed to a named cause or the row is shown to be a different failure from the other eleven, with the evidence recorded either way

**RE-SCOPED 2026-09-25 by the merger, on the slice G re-diagnosis filed below. The
clause above is kept as written and is SUPERSEDED by this paragraph.** The 262.5s gap
is UNDETERMINABLE from the evidence that survives: the one record that would settle it,
the driver's own stdout log for that night, was overwritten by a later night. The item
now requires instead that the driver's own log is RETAINED PER NIGHT, never overwritten,
so the next such gap can be diagnosed, proven by an arm in which two consecutive nights
of the driver leave two logs, each holding its own night's output.

### Full headline

lane run `62f29b90` on the 2026-09-10 night started 262.5s after its predecessor where every other gap is 47.9 to 70.4s, and left no worker log at all while being the LONGEST failing row at 3.151s - `_log_path` creates only the directory and the runner creates the file, so an absent log does not place the failure before the spawn, and a pre-spawn failure would be the fastest row rather than the slowest

### FILED 2026-09-25, from the slice G read-only re-diagnosis in wave 1 (session 113)

Filed verbatim except that its own subheadings are demoted one level to sit inside
this section, and its title line is replaced by the heading above.

Measured 2026-09-24, read-only, slice G, second attempt. The first attempt named host
memory exhaustion as the likely cause; an adversary refuted that on timing, and the
refutation is correct - see "Ruled out" below. Nothing was run against the lane.

#### Verdict

**UNDETERMINED. Neither acceptance clause is met.** The gap is not attributed to a named
cause, and the row is NOT shown to be a different failure from the other eleven - on every
measure available it is the same failure. What the evidence does settle is recorded below
so the next reader does not re-derive it.

#### Evidence read

- `ops/loop/reports/queue_loop.jsonl` (gitignored, primary checkout): the 2026-09-10 night
  is twelve rows. Cycle 1 completed; cycles 2-12 are `launch_failed`, detail
  `LaneLaunchError`, durations 2.165 to 3.151s. Run 62f29b90 is cycle 8: started
  23:25:52.394 local, ended 23:25:55.546, duration 3.151s. Cycle 7 ended 23:21:32.702.
- Gap split: start-to-start 262.5s; END of cycle 7 to START of cycle 8 is 259.7s.
- Worker logs `ops/loop/reports/lane_queue_<run_id>.log`: eleven of the twelve runs have
  one, each exactly 134 bytes (header only). Run 62f29b90 has none.
- Header-write latency (log mtime minus the row's `started_at`), cycles 2-12 in order:
  0.145, 0.152, 0.147, 0.220, 0.567, 2.037, (none), 1.984, 1.244, 1.289, 2.210s.
- Windows event logs, every log with records, 23:10-23:35 that night.
- Driver code in force that night: `ops/loop/queue_loop.py` at `dd182d7`,
  `ops/loop/lane_launcher.py` at `dd182d7`, `ops/loop/launch_queue_loop.ps1` at `e0523d8`.

#### What the driver code allows between two cycles

At `dd182d7`, between one cycle's `ended_at` and the next cycle's `started_at`, the driver
does only: `append_record` (the ledger mutex is bounded at `LEDGER_MUTEX_TIMEOUT_S` = 5.0s,
then fails open), one `print(..., flush=True)` to stdout, `sleep(settle_s)` with
`settle_s` = 45, `stop_reason` (three file-existence checks), a uuid, and `clock()`. The CI
gate's `head_sha()` runs INSIDE a cycle (after `started_at`) and after a cycle only when the
outcome is `completed`, so it is not in this interval for a `launch_failed` row. The code
therefore bounds the interval at about 50s. The observed 259.7s leaves about 214.7s that no
code path accounts for: the driver process was stalled or not scheduled.

#### Base rate

Across all 40 consecutive-cycle pairs in the ledger, unexplained time
(`next start - prev end - 45 - ci.waited_s`) is 0.7 to 1.7s on every other night, 4.7 to
22.4s in the back half of the 2026-09-10 night, and 214.7s for this one pair. It is unique.

#### Ruled out

- **Host memory exhaustion as the cause of THIS gap.** The Resource-Exhaustion-Detector
  events (System 2004, operational 1003; commit charge at 99.95 per cent of the commit
  limit), the out-of-virtual-memory popup (26) and the error-reporting service stopping on
  "paging file is too small" (7023) are at 23:28:32-33 and 23:34:36 - two minutes forty
  AFTER the gap closed, inside the gap before cycle 11. That later gap carries 22.4s of
  unexplained time, not 214.7s: heavier measured pressure produced a far smaller stall.
- **System sleep or standby.** No Kernel-Power or power-transition event in any log
  between 23:10 and 23:35.
- **A console QuickEdit freeze of the driver's output.** The driver was started by
  `launch_queue_loop.ps1` as `pythonw` with stdout and stderr redirected to files and a
  hidden window; there was no console to freeze.
- **A network wait.** No `gh` or `git` call is on the driver's path between two
  `launch_failed` cycles (see above).
- **A different failure for the row itself.** Its outcome, detail and duration match the
  other ten failed rows. Its missing log fits the same kill: header latency had already
  reached 2.04s at cycle 7 and 1.98s at cycle 9, against a kill that lands a little after
  the 2.0s grace, so a start slightly slower than its neighbours puts the kill before the
  header write. That is consistent with, not proof of, the same mechanism.

#### What remains, and why it cannot be settled now

- Events inside the gap window are only LiveId (23:23:23), Audio (23:23:59), Shell-Core
  (23:24:58), HelloForBusiness (23:25:11-12) and Crypto-NCrypt (23:25:12, 23:25:46) - signs
  of interactive activity at the machine, none of which names a stall. A lock or sign-in
  would be in the Security log, whose oldest record now postdates the night.
- A python.exe process started at 23:19:51 and was the second-largest committer at 23:28;
  header latency began climbing at cycle 6 (23:20:37). That is a correlation with rising
  load, not a cause of a 214s stall that the later, worse pressure did not reproduce.
- The one record that would settle it - the driver's own stdout log for that night - was
  overwritten; only a later driver log survives.

#### For the merger

The acceptance clause is UNMET on the evidence that exists. Either close CS-1018 as
undeterminable, recording the ruled-out list above, or re-scope it. CS-1017, merged in this
slice, makes the next such row self-describing (`launch_reason`, `launch_waited_s`), which
is the only instrument that would have discriminated this case.

## CS-1168

### Acceptance

the question is SETTLED IN WRITING before any sweep widens, and the settlement names the
boundary as a RULE rather than as a list of directories. Either outcome closes it: a
widened sweep, or a recorded declination that states what stays invisible and why. A
widened sweep must carry an arm that plants a synthetic fragment-assembled credential in
an uncommitted file INSIDE the boundary and asserts it is DETECTED, a second arm that
plants one OUTSIDE the boundary and asserts the run reports it as NOT COVERED rather than
passing silently, and a control proving the same run still detects a staged one - because
a widened population that quietly stopped reading the old one is a regression wearing a
feature's clothes. The boundary must not read a sibling tree's files. The cost must be
MEASURED and recorded, not estimated, and the fleet half must be routed outbound rather
than implemented here.

### Full headline

every credential-scanning population in this tree is REPO-SCOPED - the commit gate grades
the staged set and the repo-wide sweep grades the tracked set, so nothing here can see a
credential sitting in a file that is never committed, which is exactly where the key found
on this machine sat for ten days

### FILED 2026-09-20, as the population half of the plaintext-key incident

**THE DISTINCTION THAT MAKES THIS THE ONLY DETECTING CONTROL.** CS-1166 makes the rules
able to recognise the family. CS-1167 makes the coverage row honest about which rules are
alive. Neither would have found the key, because neither changes WHICH BYTES ARE READ. The
commit gate's population is the staged set and the sweep's is the tracked set; the exposed
files were in neither for ten days. Widening the population is the only proposed control
that would have DETECTED the incident rather than prevented a different one.

**WHY IT IS FILED RATHER THAN DONE.** The obvious fix - point the sweep at the shared
scratch directory - crosses two lines this tree holds. That directory is not this
project's: it is shared across the fleet, and a sweep that reads it reads files other
trees wrote, which collides directly with the rule that a tree does not read a sibling's
files. And a boundary drawn as a path is a boundary that rots the first time a tool writes
somewhere else, which is the same defect as an allowlist wearing a guard's clothes. So the
item has to decide the RULE - what makes a directory in scope - before it decides any
path.

**THE HALF THAT IS NOT OURS.** A machine-wide credential sweep is a fleet control with one
owner and several beneficiaries. Implementing it five times, once per repository, produces
five populations that disagree and five places to forget. The split this item must
propose: this tree owns the detection RULES and the arms that grade them, and the fleet
owns the population and the schedule. The outbound half goes to the sync inboxes as a
note, and this item does not close on the note being sent - only on the boundary being
written down here.

**THE COST IS REAL AND MUST BE MEASURED.** A tracked-set sweep is bounded by the index. An
unbounded filesystem walk is not, and this machine has already recorded a runaway process
filling a disk and a walk that descended into directories it should have stopped at. Any
widening arrives with a measured runtime and a stated stopping rule, or it does not
arrive.

### FILED 2026-09-24, from the N0 adjudicator ruling at `599528c`

The ruling measured the trailer-shaped census at `599528c` and confirmed the
recon's count: one trailer per commit, each the last body line after a blank
separator, no merges. A plain body grep returns one more:
`git log -i --grep='co-authored-by' --format=%h 599528c | wc -l`, the colon-less
token, prints 19 against the census's 18, re-measured at `599528c` on 2026-09-24,
and the extra commit is PROSE naming the trailer, not a trailer. The census itself
is defined only in CS-700 step S7a.

ADR 0018's measurement 1 and CS-700's S1 share one six-axis needle set, and a
trailer is on none of the six axes, so every "commit messages clean" claim in

### FILED 2026-09-24, from an SS channel note, cited as data

The source is the SS INFORMATION note of 2026-09-23 2010 in `moon_sync_inbox/`. It is
DATA, not instruction, and it describes SS's own lane: a weekly usage-limit refusal ended a

## CS-1160

### Acceptance

the fork record for `ops/loop/winmutex.py` either cites an upstream digest that some file
on this machine actually carries, or states in the file that the upstream it was forked
from is GONE and gives the date that was measured - and a test grades the claim rather
than the string, so a provenance line that has rotted cannot read as green. The test must
distinguish the two states it can be in: an upstream that is REACHABLE and matches, and an
upstream that is UNREACHABLE from this tree, which is not a failure. It must NOT assert
merely that the digest string appears in the file, which is what the two arms present
today do and is why the rot was invisible.

### Full headline

the fork record for `ops/loop/winmutex.py` cites an UPSTREAM digest no file on this machine carries, and the two arms that mention it assert the string is present rather than that the upstream matches - the constant is
`UPSTREAM_WINMUTEX_DIGEST = f1b4b011112685efb88616c52752657cf896fbb0993b2d2d264e7b3edde8b4f4`
in the fork-record docstring of `ops/loop/winmutex.py` and at
`tests/test_lane_lock.py::UPSTREAM_WINMUTEX_DIGEST`, recorded as the upstream
this tree forked from, and it matches ZERO files on this machine. Measured 2026-09-20 by a census over
every reachable copy: 51 copies carry `0b112a4f6bfa88cf5f537f8869225c1821ebfe97428b1e899979797ddd71a61e`,
14 carry this tree's own fork digest `e0d3ac7d9ba0be16dbe27e95354820393b9bf4edd335c97c98b39dfafb662d3f`,
and none carries `f1b4b011...`. The carriers moved their shared file and this tree's fork
record still names the version it was cut from, which no longer exists anywhere to compare
against. A sixth repository published `0b112a4f...` on the note channel on 2026-09-20 as
the current shared value, which is what prompted the census.

NO ARM BREAKS, AND THAT IS THE POINT. Nothing hashes the upstream. The two arms that
mention it - `tests/test_lane_lock.py::test_the_forked_mutex_wrapper_names_the_upstream_it_forked_from`
and `::test_the_derived_bucket_records_the_file_it_was_derived_from` - assert that the digest STRING
appears in the file's text, which is a presence check on prose. Both stay green while the
thing the prose describes ceases to exist. This is the same class as a docstring whose
behavioural claim rotted across a repair: the assertion grades the sentence, not the world
the sentence is about.

WHAT IS NOT WRONG, recorded so a reader does not go looking for a second defect. The fork
itself is sound and its own pin is correct: `sha256` of `ops/loop/winmutex.py` computed
2026-09-20 equals `tests/test_lane_lock.py::FORKED_WINMUTEX_DIGEST`, and
`python -m pytest tests/test_lane_lock.py -q` is 59 passed, exit 0. The slots digest is
also fine and was briefly mis-transcribed during this investigation: the derivation
docstring of `ops/loop/lanes.py`
and `tests/test_lane_lock.py::UPSTREAM_SLOTS_DIGEST` carry `71fa2a683f2eaa04...`, which is BYTE-EQUAL to the
value the sixth repository published, and byte-equal to the file that repository carries.
There is no slots divergence to reconcile.

THE DECISION THE FIX MUST TAKE FIRST, and why this is not a one-line digest bump. Bumping
`UPSTREAM_WINMUTEX_DIGEST` to `0b112a4f...` would be a LIE of a different shape: this tree
did not fork from that version, it forked from `f1b4b011...`. A fork record is a statement
about history, not about the present. The candidate answers are to keep the historical
digest and add a measured note that it is unreachable, or to record both - what it was cut
from, and what the carriers hold now - and say which is which. ADR 0017 owns the fork
decision and is where the answer belongs if it changes that decision's basis.

## CS-1163

### Acceptance

the citation guard sees a BARE continuation pointer - the `` `:NNN` `` form that follows a
full `path.ext:NNN` citation in the same sentence - or the repository records, in one
place with a measured count, that it deliberately does not and why. A test plants a bare
continuation beside a full pointer and asserts the guard's finding count RISES, with a
control proving the same run still detects the full pointer, so a guard that silently
stopped matching either form cannot pass. Widening the pattern is acceptable only with a
route for every site it newly reddens - the count is 67 and the largest carrier is
append-only - so the acceptance is met by a widened guard PLUS a discharged census, or by
a recorded declination that names the number.

### Full headline

the citation guard's `LINE_POINTER_RE` requires a full `path.ext:NNN`, so the BARE
continuation pointer that follows a full citation in the same sentence is invisible to it,
and 67 of them sit in the corpus today - the form is `` `:NNN` ``. Confirmed by MEASUREMENT rather
than by reading, 2026-09-20, during CS-1162: the `## CS-1160` section wrote
a full pointer at `tests/test_lane_lock.py` followed by a bare continuation, and the
guard reported the full one and NOT the continuation - while the continuation named a
live arm, `tests/test_lane_lock.py::test_the_derived_bucket_records_the_file_it_was_derived_from`.
The two offending pointers are NOT reproduced here in their original form, deliberately:
this section would otherwise carry the defect it describes, which is one of the ways the
corpus grew the other 67.
Both were repaired to symbol form under CS-1162, so the instance is gone and the BLIND
SPOT is not.

THE CENSUS, measured independently of the slice that found it, over every tracked markdown
file excluding `.git`, the channel directories and worktrees:

    42  docs/LEDGER.md                                   APPEND-ONLY, unrepairable in place
    11  docs/_scratch/cs1087_spec.md
     5  docs/history_notes.md                            HISTORICAL, unrepairable in place
     4  docs/item_notes/lane-start-failure-record.md
     2  docs/adr/0016-unlock-arrays-carriers-and-serialized-grammar.md
     1  docs/adr/0005-overclock-ceiling-source.md
     1  docs/item_notes/phase4-followups-850.md
     1  docs/item_notes/phase4-followups.md
    67  TOTAL across 8 files

**WIDENING THE REGEX WITHOUT A ROUTE FOR THOSE 67 CONVERTS A BLIND SPOT INTO AN UNPAYABLE
BILL**, which is why this is filed rather than fixed inside CS-1162. Forty-seven of the 67
are in the two carriers whose own rules forbid editing them in place, so they cannot simply
be repaired the way CS-1162 repaired the live ones. Every `ARCHIVE_ROT` pin would move at
the same time, and a pin that moves to accommodate rot is the exemption-by-convenience this
repository has already recorded against itself.

THE NUMBER IS ALSO A CORRECTION. The slice that found the blind spot reported the census as
41 in the ledger, 5 in the archive and 4 in one item-notes leaf - three files, about 50
sites. Re-measured here it is 67 across EIGHT files, and the three the slice did not name
include two ADRs and a scratch spec carrying 11 on its own. A census quoted from the file
the finder happened to be reading is not a census.

WHY THE FORM EXISTS AT ALL, because the fix is not simply "ban it". The bare continuation
is a genuine readability idiom - a full citation followed by a bare line number reads
better than repeating the path - and it is used deliberately in prose written by this project. A widened guard would
be asking authors to stop writing English. The candidate answers are therefore to widen the
pattern and require a full citation, to widen it and resolve a bare `:NNN` against the
nearest preceding path in the same sentence, or to declare the form out of scope with the
count recorded. The middle option is the only one that keeps the idiom, and it is also the
one that can mis-attribute when two different paths are cited in one sentence - which needs
its own arm.

RELATED AND DELIBERATELY NOT CLOSED BY THIS ITEM. CS-1144 is open on line-pointer rot in
`docs/LEDGER.md` for a different carrier. CS-1162 closed the symbol-citation rule into the
ledger's Entry-shape table and repaired the live instances. This item is about what the
guard can SEE, not about what the rule requires.

## CS-1179

### Acceptance

a temp-repo test drives the sequence: delete `tools/provenance.tsv`, make an honest edit
to a stamped file while it is absent, run the advised restore
`git checkout <rev> -- tools/provenance.tsv`, then the documented recovery - for example
`python tools/provenance_stamp.py rm <path>` followed by a re-`add` - and the CS-1176
re-seed arm returns green WITHOUT forgiving F1, a row that left and returned through a
re-seed, which stays red in the same run; OR the recovery is shown impossible, and the
`tools/provenance_stamp.py` docstring and the missing-manifest message say so. Proven by
mutation, with the pristine tree green in the same run.

### Full headline

### FILED 2026-09-24, from the adjudicator residuals on CS-1176

The CS-1176 re-seed arm forgives a gap in a row's manifest history only when the path's
bytes either side of the gap agree. An honest edit made while the manifest is absent
changes those bytes, so after the advised restore the row reads as one that left and
returned, and the arm is red for good. That is fail-closed, the safe direction, and the
restore advice already says to restore BEFORE editing - but a reader who did not has no
recorded way out. The adjudicator recorded that the recovery through `rm` and a re-`add`
is unproven; whether it would itself read as a row postdating the seed is NOT measured.

## CS-1176

### Acceptance

a re-seed of `tools/provenance.tsv` cannot silently launder an unstamped file into the
authored class. Either the seed refuses unless it is reconstructing exactly the rows a
committed manifest already held - so a deleted manifest is restored from history, not
re-derived - or the arm detects a re-seed by comparing the manifest against its own
committed predecessor and reddens on any row that was added without the stamp tool's
basis. Proven by mutation: delete the manifest, commit an unstamped lift, re-run the
seed, and the suite goes red naming the lift; the pristine tree is green in the same
run. The missing-manifest error message must stop recommending the seed as the fix.

### Full headline

deleting `tools/provenance.tsv` and re-running the one-time seed classifies every
unstamped file as authored, and nothing notices a re-seed

### FILED 2026-09-22, from the adversary pass that could not refute CS-1165

The seed refuses once a manifest exists, which is why the gap needs a deletion first.
The missing-manifest message tells the reader to run the seed, which is the one
instruction that turns an accident into the laundering path.

## CS-1161

### Acceptance

`moon_sync_outbox/` is covered by a `.gitignore` rule, proven by `git check-ignore -q` EXIT
CODE with a negative control that a non-ignored sibling path exits 1 in the same run - the
`-v` form is never parsed, because a sibling measured it exiting 0 with an EMPTY pattern
column on a trailing-slash argument, which reads as a match and is not one. A test asserts
the rule covers a path that DOES NOT EXIST yet as well as one that does, so the arm cannot
be satisfied by an empty directory that git declines to report. The same arm grades every
channel directory the repository carries, derived rather than hand-enumerated, so a third
one added later is covered without anyone remembering to add a row.

### Full headline

`moon_sync_outbox/` is untracked AND carries no `.gitignore` rule, so a `git add -A` commits
cross-repo correspondence into a repository whose phase 7 gate is a public flip. Measured
2026-09-20 by exit code with a control: `git check-ignore -q moon_sync_inbox` exits 0
against `.gitignore:282`, and `git check-ignore -q moon_sync_outbox` exits 1. The directory
is not hypothetical and not empty - it held three delivered notes at the moment this was
filed, so `git status --porcelain` reports `?? moon_sync_outbox/` today.

THE ASYMMETRY IS THE DEFECT, not the missing line on its own. The INBOX is ignored and the
OUTBOX is not, which means the half of the channel this tree AUTHORS is the unprotected
half. Everything in the outbox was written by CS about CS, which is exactly the content a
public flip most needs to have been a deliberate decision rather than a default.

A SIBLING PREDICTED THIS SHAPE AND CS IS PAST THE POINT IT WARNED ABOUT. LW filed the same
finding against its own root `worktrees/` on 2026-09-19: invisible to git only because git
does not report empty directories, and "the moment anything lands in it, it becomes
untracked content in a public repository with no ignore rule behind it". LL filed the
identical shape against `.backtest/` and `.claude/worktrees/` the same day. **In all three
sibling cases the directory was EMPTY and the finding was anticipatory. CS's is populated.**
The generalisable part is LL's: an orphaned empty directory is reported by exactly ONE of
the four enumeration commands, so a sweep that runs only `git status --ignored` returns a
clean bill that is a claim about git's reporting rule rather than about the tree - and once
the directory fills, the same tree that looked clean starts offering its contents to the
next `git add -A`.

WHY THE TEST MUST USE A NON-EXISTENT PATH. The arm that would most naturally be written -
check-ignore against the outbox as it stands - passes for the wrong reason on a machine
where the directory happens to be absent, because a directory-only rule cannot match a path
git cannot see is a directory. LW measured that exact false RED in a throwaway repository.
Grading a path that does not exist, and a path that does, in the same arm is what separates
the rule's presence from the filesystem's state.

WHAT THIS ITEM IS NOT. It is not a proposal to track the outbox, and not a proposal to
delete it. The channel's own convention is that both directories are untracked because a
note is correspondence between checkouts on one machine rather than project history. This
item makes the untracked half of that convention enforced instead of accidental.

## CS-1159

### Acceptance

every command in `hooks.PreToolUse` and `hooks.PostToolUse` in `.claude/settings.json`
whose token ends in `.py` resolves from a root that is not the process working directory,
and a test proves it by spawning that command with `cwd` set to an explicitly supplied
foreign directory rather than to the runner's own - so the arm reads the same in the
primary tree, in a worktree and under xdist. The arm that grades the DEFECT asserts on the
`can't open file` MESSAGE and not on the exit code, because exit 2 is not self-evidencing.
The arm that grades the REPAIR carries both halves: a benign envelope from that foreign cwd
exits 0, AND a real violation from the same cwd is still denied - the second half is the
control, because an anchor that also disarmed the gate would satisfy the first half alone.
A structural arm generalises past the two strings present today and refuses a hardcoded
drive-letter root or home-directory segment, so non-negotiable 3 is not traded for
cwd-independence.

### Full headline

`.claude/settings.json` wires both hook commands by a CWD-RELATIVE path, so a session whose working directory moves loses the gate and, for PreToolUse, every shell - `pythonw tools/pretooluse_gate.py` at line 20
and `python tools/edit_lint_check.py` at line 32, both resolved off the repository root. Measured 2026-09-20 at `b039a49`:
after the session cwd moved to `C:\Clockspeed\moon_sync_inbox` while reading the note
channel, every Bash and PowerShell call in the main session AND in four separately
dispatched subagents was DENIED before executing, with `can't open file
'C:\Clockspeed\moon_sync_inbox\tools\pretooluse_gate.py'`. Subagents inherit the session
cwd, so the blast radius is not the session that moved. The four each lost their shell for
their whole run and returned explicit UNVERIFIABLE verdicts: between them not one sha256,
byte count, mtime, `git worktree list`, `git log -S` or `git check-ignore` exit code was
obtainable. A bare `pwd` was refused, and `cd /c/Clockspeed && <cmd>` was refused too,
because the hook fires BEFORE the command - so the shell cannot recover itself and
recovery took a non-shell tool.

It DEFEATS THE WRAPPER'S OWN WRITTEN CONTRACT, which is what makes it a defect rather than
fail-closed working as designed. The fail-open half of the two-part contract stated in the
module docstring of `tools/pretooluse_gate.py` promises exit 0 on the
wrapper's own error, on the stated grounds that "a convenience layer that bricks every
shell call is far worse than one that misses, and the commit path is protected by
.githooks regardless". That branch is UNREACHABLE when the script is never entered:
CPython's own exit 2 for a missing file reaches the harness first and the harness reads
hook exit 2 as DENY. Fail-closed here therefore buys zero commit-path safety, because
`.githooks/*` and `tools/precommit_gate.py` are the authoritative Tier-0 gates and are
untouched either way.

THE TWO LINES FAIL DIFFERENTLY, and the quieter one is the worse class. Line 20 denies
loudly. Line 32 did not bite at all, because Edit and Write need no shell and a PostToolUse
non-zero exit does not deny - so from a stale cwd the lint check simply never runs and
nothing says so. That is a false guarantee, which this project rates worse than the bug it
hides, and it is the reason line 32 is inside this item rather than deferred.

A RULE WAS REJECTED AS THE CONTROL, on evidence rather than taste. CLAUDE.md and the
harness memory index ALREADY carry "Inbox review includes subdirectories ... Never cd into
one", and it did not prevent this. A control whose cost is unbounded in the blast radius of
a routine slip is not adequately handled by restating the slip.

FROZEN FILE. `.claude/settings.json` is on the CLAUDE.md section 6 list. The adjudicator
grant, its scope, the rejected alternatives and the named residual are recorded in
`docs/LEDGER.md` under CS-1159, filed BEFORE the edit as section 6 requires.

THE RESIDUAL, which the acceptance above deliberately does NOT close. Every strand
supporting `$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` traces to ONE upstream input, the Claude Code client's
expansion behaviour, so the sibling repositories using it and the agents proposing it are
downstream readers rather than independent witnesses. The acceptance arms expand the
variable THEMSELVES, so they grade the command string's cwd-independence and not whether
this harness expands it. The harness half is settled only by observation: from a
deliberately moved cwd, one violating call denied with the gate's OWN stderr - proving the
script was reached and ran rather than never found - then one benign call that runs.

OUT OF SCOPE, recorded so it is not mistaken for covered. `.claude/settings.local.json`
carries the identical relative path for its `SessionStart` hook. It is gitignored, so no
grant reaches it and no tracked test can pin it. Also unmeasured: whether a worktree's
`$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` resolves to the worktree or to the primary, which decides whether a
lane session gates against its own tree.

## CS-920 - item section, CLOSED and relocated from `docs/item_notes/phase4-followups-900.md` 2026-09-17


### FILED 2026-09-06 (session 65) by the merger, from an idea another project on this machine raised for itself

**THE IDEA, AND WHERE IT CAME FROM.** A sibling project asked whether numbers it DERIVES and
then COMMITS would be read by an outsider as no different from wiki content. Its answer
split in two, and only the second half transfers here.

**THE FIRST HALF DOES NOT APPLY TO THIS PROJECT AND THAT IS WORTH STATING so nobody files
it again.** That project transcribes measurements into tracked tables. This one does not:
`/data/` is gitignored, the registry is extracted from the game's shipped files AT RUNTIME,
and CS-485 settled that no dataset is lifted from any wiki. There is no committed game
number here for an outsider to lift, so the wiki-equivalence question does not arise.

**THE SECOND HALF APPLIES SHARPLY, AND TO THIS PROJECT'S MEASUREMENTS OF ITSELF.** Its
formulation is that provenance which is DOCUMENT-scoped does not survive the number being
quoted: an outside reader lifts the row, not the document, and the receipt is left behind.
The same failure happens INSIDE this repository, between sessions, without anyone lifting
anything - because a number quoted out of its paragraph loses the conditions it was taken
under, and the next session requotes it as fact.

**MEASURED, IN THIS SESSION ALONE. Three numbers were published and then corrected:**

- a **3.2x** speedup, from comparing readings taken at different times on a contended box,
  corrected to **2.39x** by a paired back-to-back re-measurement. That was the THIRD
  unpaired-comparison error recorded against CS-896.
- **sixteen workers**, which is **eight** - xdist counts physical cores. The evidence was
  present twice before the correction: a builder reported eight, and a failure signature
  read `workers=9`, being eight workers plus one misfiled controller.
- a **shard-specific** variance claim, withdrawn once an adversary showed an identical
  runner pool reproduces the contrast about one time in three.

None of those was a careless reading. Each was a correct reading whose CONDITIONS did not
travel with it.

**THE ITEM EXISTS BECAUSE CS-917 ALREADY DEPENDS ON THE ANSWER.** Its acceptance asks for
"a noise figure that survives its own next reading". **That is a QUERY over a measurement
history**, and today there is no history to query - the readings for CS-896 alone are spread
across roughly seven ledger entries, an item note and a workflow comment, in prose, with
their conditions stated in sentences. A session cannot mechanically ask "was this reading
taken on a quiet box" or "which readings has a later one falsified".

**WHAT THE RECEIPT HAS TO CARRY**, derived from the three corrections above rather than
guessed: the metric and its value and unit; the METHOD (paired or unpaired, standalone or
through the real gate); the worker count actually resolved rather than the core count; the
LOAD STATE, because "another project's suite was live" is the condition that produced two of
the three errors; the date and the commit; and whether a later reading has superseded it.

**WHAT THIS IS NOT.** It is not a benchmarking harness and it is not CodSpeed. It records
readings a human or a session already took, so they can be compared later. And it is not a
licence question: facts are not copyrightable, so no licence on this repository protects a
number in it - what distinguishes a measurement from a rumour is the receipt, not the terms.

**RELATION TO EXISTING DOCTRINE.** `CLAUDE.md` section 4 already says "do not restate a
measured number in prose" and requires one machine-checked owner per fact. That rule is
enforced today only for a few specific numbers - the tier 1 levels, by drift guard (k) and

## CS-919 - item section, CLOSED and relocated from `docs/item_notes/phase4-followups-900.md` 2026-09-17


**Filed 2026-09-06 by the merger, out of CS-918's first real cycle.** Read that closure
entry in `docs/LEDGER.md` first - this item exists because of something the cycle did, not
because of something someone thought might happen.

### WHAT WAS MEASURED

The driver reads `origin/main` before the cycle and again after it, and treats a change as
"our worker pushed". On the first real cycle the worker committed NOTHING - it left ten
files uncommitted in the lane worktree - while another session on the same box pushed
`f80b95af7e2e`. The driver saw the ref move, attributed it to the cycle, waited out tier1,
**dispatched a tier2 run**, and waited 1105.9 seconds for it. The row records
`"ci": {"verdict": "success"}` against a sha the lane never produced.

### WHY THIS IS WORSE THAN IT LOOKS

It is silent, and it fails in BOTH directions. A neighbour's green is written into this
lane's ledger as though the lane had earned it - and a neighbour's RED would stop the night
under `ci_red`, blaming a worker that pushed nothing. Neither shows up as an error; both
read as ordinary rows. The ledger is the only durable record of a night, so a row that
cites the wrong sha is worse than a row that cites none.

### WHAT IS NOT THE FIX

**Do not narrow the window.** The window is the whole cycle - tens of minutes by design -
and any attempt to shrink it trades a large silent error for a smaller silent error.

**Do not assume one lane per box.** That is the assumption that produced this. The operator
runs several projects' sessions concurrently on this machine; the measurement above is that
configuration behaving normally, not an anomaly.

### THE SHAPE OF AN ANSWER

The lane can know what its own worker produced without asking the remote: the worker commits
in a worktree the driver owns the path of, so the driver can read `lane/queue`'s tip before
and after and compare THAT, or read the reflog of the branch it launched into. A sha the
lane cannot attribute to itself must record `unattributable` and grade nothing - an absent
verdict is a real answer, and it is the one CS-918's own driver already gives when the
remote cannot be resolved.

### THE ARM THAT PROVES IT

Redden on a FOREIGN sha landing between the two reads. A test that only checks the happy
path would have passed on the shipped code, because the shipped code is correct whenever
nobody else pushes - which is every run on an idle box and no run on this one.

## CS-1068 - item section, CLOSED and relocated from `docs/item_notes/phase4-followups-900.md` 2026-09-16

### Filed 2026-09-14 as the residual of CS-828's partial ship

**WHAT CS-828 SHIPPED AND WHAT IT LEFT.** `read_trailing_run` reads the int32 the run
OPENS with, out of the bytes, on every payload of every pair in `TRAILING_RUN_PAIRS`, and
`TrailingRun.unread` carries the width of everything past it. On the large majority of
payloads that remainder is zero and the run is fully read. On the rest it is not, and this
item owns the rest. The counts are not restated here - `tests/save/test_trailing_run.py`
derives them on every run and `docs/LEDGER.md` records what was observed the day it
shipped.

**THE REMAINDER IS CLASS-KEYED, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE DIFFICULTY.** It is not keyed by the
version pair, so no single grammar reads it: one class writes a count prefix followed by
that many records, another writes a pair of length-prefixed strings, another writes
neither. **DO NOT PROPOSE A PAIR-WIDE GRAMMAR FOR IT.** A reading that dispatched on the
version pair would have to be right for every class at once, and the corpus already
falsifies that.

**THE FENCE THAT MATTERS MOST, AND IT IS THE ONE THAT REFUTED CS-830 AFTER IT HAD MERGED.**
The remainder's width is whatever the bytes are, so ANY partition of it closes by
arithmetic and no reading of it could have failed. A slice that splits the remainder into
named regions summing to `declared_end - terminator_end` has measured nothing, however
many tests it ships. The acceptance therefore asks for a reading whose width comes from
something SELF-DESCRIBING inside the run - a count prefix, or a length-prefixed string -
and asks for an arm that reddens when that derivation is swapped for the observed width.
**A SLICE THAT CANNOT SHOW THAT ARM RED HAS NOT MET THE CLAUSE.**

**THE CLASS IS DERIVED, NEVER TRANSCRIBED.** This project has recorded repeatedly that a
hand-maintained vocabulary of game content is the thing that rots, and CS-829's own note
forbids exactly this shape of transcription. Pick the class off the corpus at test time
the way `tests/save/test_struct_interior.py` derives its struct vocabulary, so a corpus
that stops carrying it says so rather than going quietly green.

**SCOPE IS ONE CLASS, DELIBERATELY.** The clause asks for `unread` to fall to zero on
exactly one derived class's payloads and nowhere else. That is a bounded row that can ship
in a cycle and a measurable step, and the "and nowhere else" half is what stops a reader
that returns zero for everything from passing. Widening it to every class at once is how
this becomes the item that absorbs a night and ships nothing.

**NOT THE STRUCT INTERIOR AND NOT THE (14,60) PAIR.** `StructProperty`'s interior is
CS-829 and carries its own six fences. The (14,60) pair reaches no property terminator at
all, so it has no trailing run to read and stays scoped into CS-G05; `TRAILING_RUN_PAIRS`
is derived so that the pair cannot drift into this item's population by editing a list.

## CS-1060 - RELOCATED 2026-09-14 on closure, from docs/item_notes/phase4-followups-900.md

**CLOSED. The ledger entry dated 2026-09-14 is the record; this is the working note it was
built from, moved here because `docs/item_notes/` holds live detail for OPEN work only.**

**WHAT THE NOTE GOT RIGHT.** It refused to let the gate be repaired by moving a threshold, and
it was arithmetic rather than preference: solving the feasibility rule at the then-observed
spread ratio put the requirement near 320 seconds, roughly 1.6x below where the lane sat.
The remedy it named - a third shard plus real trimming - is what shipped.

**WHAT IT GOT WRONG, AND IT MATTERS MORE THAN WHAT IT GOT RIGHT.** The note assumed the slow
runner class was the one a short sample would MISS. A 24-run class model built at adjudication
time says the opposite: the slow class is about 78 per cent of draws, so a tight cluster at the
top of the distribution IS the slow class rather than an unsampled one. A session reading this
note alone would draw the wrong conclusion from three green readings.


### Filed 2026-09-14

**THIS IS THE ENABLING ITEM FOR A WALL-CLOCK GATE AND IT DETECTS NOTHING BY ITSELF.**
Solving the published feasibility rule at the observed spread ratio `N/M = 222/511 =
0.4345` gives `M'(1 + 0.869) <= 600`, so `M' <= 321`. **A wall-clock gate becomes feasible
again only if the slow-class worst job reading drops to about 320 seconds**, roughly 1.6x
below where the lane sits today. That is a third shard plus real trimming, not a tuning
change, and it fights the leanness rule stated at the top of `.github/workflows/tier1.yml`.

**IT IS FILED SEPARATELY BECAUSE THE RISK IT CARRIES BELONGS TO NOBODY TODAY.** The
runaway cutoff sits at 10 minutes and CANCELS rather than fails; a cancelled run is
evidence of nothing and reads to the next session as flakiness. At 511 job-seconds the
slow class is 89 seconds from that cutoff, and CS-1012's own repair ADDS 20 to 40 seconds
to the job. Whoever builds CS-1012 first without this one walks the lane into a
cancellation.

**DO NOT REACH FOR THE CUTOFF.** `tier1.yml` states in capitals that raising it converts a
runaway detector into a budget, and `tools/drift_guard.py` guard (k) pins it as policy
rather than reading it as a tunable, so any change up or down is red until the pin moves
in the same diff with a stated reason. The remedy here is a shorter lane, never a longer
leash.

  SESSION. `docs/GATED.md` recorded under CS-G05 that a `(14,60)` save decodes zero
  property tags and "cannot exercise the decoder at all - it is the CONTROL". The operator
  showed a third-party interactive map rendering container contents out of a save on this
  machine. Same file, same pair. The zero was real and reproduced on demand; the inference
  from it was wrong. A save that decodes nothing under ONE grammar is not a save that
  carries nothing. `CLAUDE.md` section 8 decided it: the probe wins, the gate is corrected.

- Surprises: the wall was BOTH candidates at once, which is why neither alone closed it -
  a lead byte the reader did not skip AND a tag grammar it did not know. Four readings were
  driven against the whole population before one read every record with no breaks. A
  plausible fix and a correct one look identical on a single record.

- Surprises: an adversary was dispatched to refute the zero-properties finding and did not
  refute it - but corrected its WORDING in the way that mattered. The finding had been
  stated as a defect on the production dashboard path; it was neither path-specific nor
  novel, and `docs/GATED.md` already held it. Being right about the fact and wrong about
  its standing is the failure mode to watch for here.

- Surprises: the built-class allowlist was seeded from the only `Build_*_C` spellings in
  the tree, which came out of an ARCHIVED spike report - and three of those nine were the
  only ones present in the operator's world. The map plotted 37 of 698 built actors. A

## CS-884 - item section, closed and relocated from `docs/item_notes/phase4-followups-850.md` 2026-09-02

### NOTE - filed 2026-09-01 (session 56) by the merger, MEASURED BY PLANTING FIVE SHAPES

**THE CENSUS HAS NO VERDICT THAT MEANS REPAIRED.** `classify` returns `MEASURED_LEAK`,

site CS-857 has ever repaired lands in `UNPROVEN`.

**WHAT UNPROVEN ACTUALLY HOLDS, planted and measured.** Five shapes through
`sites_in_tree`, one module each:

    positional no-op  _id(exc)      -> measured-leak   CAUGHT
    keyword no-op     _id(e=exc)    -> unproven        escapes
    lambda no-op                    -> unproven        escapes
    two-step forward                -> unproven        escapes
    genuine clone                   -> unproven        correct, and indistinguishable

and the verdict does not say which. That is limit 10 stated as a consequence rather than as
a caveat.

**IT IS A LATENT HAZARD, NOT A LIVE LEAK - do not inflate this.** Swept on the same day: no
shipped module uses any of the three escaping shapes. The shipped `UNPROVEN` population is
project-exception causes, suppressed raises, genuine clones, and two benign alternate
spellings - `clockspeed/data/blobs.py` chaining a `ValueError` from `int()`, and
