## CS-1041

### Filed 2026-09-13

**FOUR QUESTIONS, ONE CAUSE.** Which belt feeds which machine, which node a miner sits on,
which connections share a power circuit, and whether a machine is running are all answered
by references and per-machine properties that the decoder already recovers and the world
seam already drops. The mechanism is verified - an `ObjectProperty` value decodes, and
`RecordIndex.records_for` resolves an object path to every record bearing that name.

**WRITE-LIST:** NEW `network` and `machines` modules under `clockspeed/audit/`, and one
NEW arm module under `tests/audit/` for each of them. **DEPENDS ON:** CS-1039.
**TIER 2, NO GAME NEEDED.** **PUBLISHES:** `WorldNetwork` - mined node keys, belt and pipe
edges keyed by an INDEX into the placement population and NEVER by instance name, circuit
membership, and the counts that are its own denominators; `WorldMachines` - per-record
recipe, producing flag and overclock, each behind a declared availability flag.

**A PROXIMITY FALLBACK IS FORBIDDEN.** Non-negotiable 7 forbids it by name: nearest-neighbour
renders a wrong answer that reads like a right one. The acceptance arm must REDDEN when the
reference join is replaced by nearest-neighbour, or it grades nothing.

**ASSUMED, NOT MEASURED:** that a miner carries an ObjectProperty naming its node actor. The
MECHANISM is verified; the PROPERTY NAME is not. Measure it before building on it.

**A CORRECTION THIS ITEM CARRIES, BECAUSE IT IS A REFUTATION OF A SESSION-85 SPIKE CLAIM.**
A spike reported that CS-405 "probes the wrong field" because `mInventoryPotential` is an
ObjectProperty resolving to an inventory component rather than the overclock float. **That
correction was already known and the spike's claim is REFUTED.** Verified this session by
reading the module: `tests/save/test_inventory_potential.py`'s module docstring, under
its heading WHAT THE TAG WAS ALREADY MEASURED TO BE, already records that
`mInventoryPotential` decodes as an ObjectProperty - a level string and an object path - and
not as a bare integer, and states that this refutes the naive reading of YES without
establishing NO because a count may live BEHIND the reference; ADR 0009 records what the
experiment found and CS-831 shipped the reference following the module consumes. CS-405 is
CLOSED and its body is in `docs/history_notes.md`; no item is filed against it and nothing
in it needs repair. **The USEFUL half of the spike survives and lands here:** the live
overclock values are `mCurrentPotential` and `mPendingPotential`, measured 2026-09-13 at
five records each, and those are the fields this item reads. An ABSENT `mCurrentPotential`
is published as null and NEVER as 1.

**`mHasBeenLooted` IS SPARSE AND ITS ABSENCE MEANS DEFAULT-FALSE.** Read as "unknown" it
makes a plain unlooted pod unmeasurable; read as false it is correct. The model states which
reading it took rather than leaving it to a reader.

**BELT PATH GEOMETRY IS OUT OF SCOPE AND THAT IS NOT A DEFERRAL.** `mSplineData` and
`mSplinePoints` decode to zero elements today and are unblocked only by CS-1038. The
red-outline requirement needs the GRAPH, not the path. Belts render endpoint-to-endpoint and
the model declares `spline_geometry_available` false.

## CS-1042

### Filed 2026-09-13

**THE POLARITY IS COLLECTED, AND EVERY LATER READER MUST BE TOLD SO BEFORE THEY NAME A
FIELD.** The save's collectable section records what has ALREADY BEEN COLLECTED, as
(level, actor instance) pairs. Measured 2026-09-13: 72 pairs, none of which matches a live
record - which is exactly what identifies the polarity. **UNCOLLECTED is the live records
carrying transforms MINUS those pairs.** An agent that reads the section as a list of
uncollected items has it backwards. Live uncollected records carry transforms and are the
crystal classes and their marks, the spawnable pickups, the drop pods, the crash-site debris
and the resource deposits; the collected stems seen in the pairs are a different and
non-overlapping population.

**WRITE-LIST:** a NEW `collectibles` module under `clockspeed/audit/`, and one NEW arm
module for it under `tests/audit/`. **DEPENDS ON:** CS-1038 for the pairs and CS-1039 for the seam. **TIER 2, NO GAME NEEDED.**
**PUBLISHES:** `WorldCollectibles` - one row per uncollected item with its transform,
per-class counts, a skipped count, and a `collected_state_available` flag.

**THE ACCEPTANCE GRADES THE SUBTRACTION, NOT THE PLOTTING.** This is the single
highest-vacuity-risk arm in the session. An arm asserting only that three collectibles
render PASSES on an implementation that ignores the collected list entirely, which is the
whole defect. The arm must redden when the subtraction is removed.

**THE CLASS FILTER IS AN ALLOWLIST AND NEVER A DENYLIST**, authored from the measured stems,
with a PUBLISHED skipped count. A denylist on this project leaked four times - one defect
wore four spellings across four GREEN commits - and only an allowlist of good values held.
A skipped class is COUNTED, never silently dropped.

**ASSERT PER CLASS, NOT OVER THE POOL.** A threshold summed over a population is met by its
strongest member while the weakest goes unmeasured with the acceptance clause still passing.

**THE SAVE LIBRARY MOVES WHILE YOU WORK, so no acceptance here may state a hardcoded save
count.** The operator plays while agents run: the record total was probed twice inside one
session on 2026-09-13 and had moved between the two reads. A count written into a test is a
lie with a timestamp on it (`CLAUDE.md` section 4). Every equality below is over a
population DERIVED from the payload being read, compared against the reader's own output,
never against a literal.

## CS-1045

### Filed 2026-09-13

**TWO REQUIREMENTS WITH NO NUMBER BEHIND THEM.** `/api/power` answers for ONE building
against the registry alone with no world bound into it, nothing multiplies a per-class draw
by a built count, and no rule anywhere compares a machine's input to its output.

**WRITE-LIST:** a NEW `balance` module under `clockspeed/audit/`, and one NEW arm
module for it under `tests/audit/`. **DEPENDS ON:** CS-1041. **TIER 2, NO GAME NEEDED** - synthetic registry and synthetic
world. **PUBLISHES:** `WorldBalance` - production and consumption, an unmodeled-contributor
count, the imbalanced record set, and the connected edge set the panel outlines red.

**THE CONFIDENT ZERO IS THE FAILURE MODE HERE.** `clockspeed/solve/power.py`'s unmodeled
cases must EACH contribute a NAMED gap to the total and never a zero. `contract.encode`
refuses a float; a zero it happily accepts, and a zero is a lie a power plan cannot detect.
This is the silently-wrong half of non-negotiable 7 wearing a number.

**ASSERT PER CONTRIBUTOR, NOT OVER THE POOL.** A total that is correct in aggregate can hide
a class whose draw was never modelled; the arm must name the gap rather than measure the sum
alone.

**THE WHOLE-WORLD PAIR DOES NOT NEED THE CIRCUIT GRAPH** and is what this item ships. The
per-circuit split does need it and is a stated stretch, recorded here so a later reader does
not mistake its absence for an oversight.

### FILED 2026-09-06 (session 70). THE PREMISE THAT SENT THE PROBE WAS REFUTED, AND SO WAS THE LEDGER

The session-69 handoff asked whether the shipped docs file exposes build cost at
all, and warned that if it does not, `BOOTSTRAP.md` carries an unlabelled
assumption and CLAUDE.md section 8 applies. **It does expose it.** The item that
remains is a join, not an acquisition.

### WHAT WAS MEASURED, against the real install

- **There is no `mBuildCost` key. Zero occurrences.** That naive lookup is what
  made this look absent, and it is why the earlier note was written.
- Build cost is carried on the BUILD GUN RECIPES. Of 872 `FGRecipe` entries,
  550 name a build gun in `mProducedIn` and **545 carry a non-empty
  `mIngredients`**. `Recipe_ConstructorMk1_C` inputs are reinforced iron plate
  x2 and cable x8 - that is the Constructor's build cost.
- **It is already inside this project's registry.** A real build yields
  items=750, recipes=872, buildings=68, and all 550 build recipes are present as
  `Recipe` objects with `inputs` populated, tagged
  `unresolved_produced_in=('BP_BuildGun_C',)`, which `clockspeed/data/registry.py`
  already names as a tolerated token.
- **`clockspeed/data/registry.py::automated_recipes` returns 291 and filters all
  550 out.** Correct for its purpose, and the reason they are invisible
  downstream.
- **65 of 68** modelled Buildings have a build recipe whose output joins by
  `Desc_` to `Build_` substitution. The three that do not are part of the item.

### THE EXISTING RECORD IS WRONG AND MUST NOT BE INHERITED

the CS-922 entry in `docs/LEDGER.md` states build "COST DATA DOES NOT EXIST AT ALL" and that
"the docs extractor never reads one". The first clause is FALSE and the second
is FALSE - the extractor reads `KEY_INGREDIENTS` for all 872 recipes including
all 550 build recipes. Only "`Building` has no cost field" is true.

The ledger is append-only, so that entry is not edited; a correction is appended
beside the CS-930 filing rather than written over it.

### WHAT THIS ITEM IS NOT

It is not a data-acquisition problem and must not be scoped as one. It is a join
plus an aggregation over data already loaded. Do not re-pitch extracting build
cost from a wiki or any community source - `CLAUDE.md` section 7 settles that,
and the data is on disk anyway.

## 2026-09-18 - CS-1145 - RETIRED ITEM SECTION, relocated here when the item closed (session 105)

Relocated from `docs/item_notes/phase4-followups-1000.md` when the item closed.
The completion record is in `docs/LEDGER.md`. Nothing here is current.

### FILED 2026-09-18, from the windows-latest leg of tier 2 run 35330059133

**WHAT WENT RED, AND WHAT DID NOT.** One leg of one job:
`tests/test_tier1_budget.py::test_a_run_inside_the_budget_reports_it_and_succeeds`
asserted `393 <= 390 + 2` and failed. The ubuntu leg of the same job passed, both
clean-checkout probes passed and both shell suites passed. NOTHING IN
`.github/workflows/tier1.yml` WAS WRONG, and this item must not be closed by
touching it - guard (k) ratchets its levels in both directions for exactly the
reason that a number moved to quiet a red is a number nobody defended.

**THE MECHANISM.** The report step computes `ELAPSED=$(( $(date +%s) -
TIER1_STARTED ))`. The arm stages `TIER1_STARTED` as a Python clock read minus
the duration it wants, then spawns bash. The figure the step reports is therefore
the staged duration PLUS the wall clock that passed between the harness reading
its clock and the shell reading its own. On a loaded windows runner that cost
three seconds; the arm allowed two. The arm was measuring a gap it did not own.

**WHY A BIGGER NUMBER IS THE WRONG REPAIR, AND THIS FILE ALREADY HOLDS THE
EVIDENCE.** The comment block in `.github/workflows/tier1.yml` records TWO
derivations of that lane's band that were falsified by the very run offered to
close them, and CS-1133 and CS-1134 are open about the third. A tolerance is a
claim about a machine nobody measured. Worse, a wide one stops proving the thing
the arm exists to prove: the arm's job is to show the reported figure DERIVES
from the staged start, and a thirty-second window is satisfied by a step that
ignores the staged start entirely whenever the true figure happens to land inside
it.

**MEASURING THE GAP LOCALLY PRODUCES THE WRONG ANSWER, WHICH IS THE POINT.** Ten
readings taken while filing this item reported the staged figure EXACTLY, gap
zero every time - because this machine was idle. Any constant derived from that
measurement would have been undersized against CI again, the same way the two
falsified derivations above were produced from single samples.

**SO THE READING IS BRACKETED RATHER THAN TOLERATED.** The clock is read before
the spawn and again after it returns. `floor` is monotonic, so the shell's own
read lies between those two, and the reported figure can be no less than the
staged duration and no more than `later_read - started`. That is an arithmetic
fact about the run that just happened, not an estimate of a runner: a slow runner
WIDENS the bracket instead of breaking it, and on a fast one the bracket closes
to nothing. `report_with_bounded_reading` in `tests/test_tier1_budget.py` owns it.

**THE ANTI-VACUITY CONTROL IS AN ARM RATHER THAN A ONE-OFF CHECK.**
`test_a_slow_harness_does_not_push_the_reading_outside_what_the_clock_allows`
injects the three-second gap CI measured and asserts BOTH that the reading leaves
the two-second window this item removed AND that the bracket still holds over it.
Without the first conjunct the arm would be green on an idle machine for the same
reason the machine is idle, which is the vacuity this repository has filed twice.

**WHAT THE MUTANTS DID, MEASURED, BOTH DIRECTIONS.** Against a step whose
`ELAPSED` is hardcoded to the figure the within-budget arm stages, the stall arm
and the over-budget arm are RED and the within-budget arm alone is GREEN - the
bracket cannot separate a constant from a derivation when the constant equals the
staged value, and that is why the other two arms stage a different duration and a
different gap. Against a step reading only `date +%s`, all three are RED. Pristine
is GREEN before and after each mutation, with the workflow restored from a byte
snapshot rather than from git.

**WHY TIER 2 ON A TEST-ONLY DIFF.** The close condition is a reading off the live
lane, not a local module run: the arm was green on every local run of the shape
that failed in CI.

### Acceptance

the two duration arms in `tests/test_tier1_budget.py` bound the reported figure
against clocks the arm reads itself around the spawn rather than against any
fixed allowance, no arm in that module carries a constant tolerance for the
harness-to-shell gap, an arm reproduces the measured three-second gap and is red
if that gap fails to land, the repaired arms are refuted by a step whose figure
does not derive from `TIER1_STARTED` and are green against the shipped step, and
the windows-latest leg of tier 2 is observed green on a commit carrying this
change with `.github/workflows/tier1.yml` unmodified

## Session 106 - 2026-09-19 - two rows ran, one closed and one was refuted by an adversary, and the publication gate got its first real closure scan

**CLOSED: CS-1147, CS-1146. REFUTED AND STILL OPEN: CS-900. FILED: CS-1152.**

**CS-1147 - the ration arm no longer races the child it measures.** The child called
`ration.release()` and THEN wrote its released marker, so a parent acquiring in that
window saw two of three protocol signals. Reproduced FIRST by widening the gap to 0.5s,
which gave the byte-identical CI assertion; the same widening passes after the reorder.
Then an adversary refuted my own done-claim on the first commit: I had verified teeth with
a LIVE never-releasing child (red in 124.89s) and called the clause discharged, but the
CANONICAL mutant - delete the release call, change nothing else - was GREEN in 0.15s both
before and after. The child EXITED the instant it stopped holding and the ration correctly
reclaims a dead holder's slot, so nothing in the arm told a release from a death. The child
now waits for a `parent_done` dismissal written after the measurement, so it is alive across
the parent's acquire. That mutant now fails in 120.33s. The same pass found a SECOND race of
the same family: `_await_file` returned the instant a path existed, and `write_text`
truncates before it writes, so both process arms could read an empty marker and die in
`int()` with an uncaught ValueError. It waits for a byte now.

**CS-1146 - and session 105's caveat against itself was WRONG ON ITS OWN NUMBER.** That
caveat de-ranked the row because "the very next tier 1 run had the guard shard at 230s".
Measured from the jobs API: that run was 413s and the next was 441s. With the record's 11
readings at 426-464, that is 12 of 13 known readings at or over the 420s budget, spread 38s.
The caveat's METHOD was right - measure the spread before ranking - and following it
reversed its own conclusion. `tools/tier1_growth.py` now grades `B >= M` per job as a verdict
distinct from the band-versus-jitter one, names each job with its own margin, and prints
BUDGET BREACHED by 44s over the shipped record. No level moved.

**CS-900 SHIPPED ITS TOOL AND STILL FAILED, on an adversary and not on my reading.** Two
counter-examples. (1) The save shard WARNS at both ends of the profile with the SAME top
test across four commits that touched only another job, so branch one closes only by
electing the LOOSER of two stated shares - and the 18.9 per cent concentration that FILED
the item passes the 50 per cent hard level. A level under which the filed defect passes
cannot be the level the close rests on. (2) The hard level's derivation was FALSE: the
`t_max <= T/W` criterion is against the SERIAL TOTAL and the tool divides by the STEP WALL
CLOCK, which agree only at one worker. Corrected in the docstring, not dropped. `T` is not
obtainable from a block printing only the top 15 phases over 5s, so that criterion cannot be
graded by this tool at all.

**THE PUBLICATION GATE GOT ITS FIRST REAL CLOSURE SCAN, and six of seven axes are CLEAR.**
Over everything reachable from `main`: 1059 commits, 3255 blobs, 461 DISTINCT HISTORICAL
PATH STRINGS - 42 more than HEAD, which is the half that leaks. No account id, no standalone
world name, no home paths, no save bytes, no game assets, no `data/` or inbox payload, in
ANY commit. The one finding is the plan's own credential allowlist drifting against its own
synthetic canaries, and the plan sentence asserting the real token prefixes return zero is

the tree, and was graded by RESTORING rather than by verifying.

**PROCESS FINDINGS - MEASURED, DO NOT REDISCOVER.**

- A CONTENDED xdist SUITE REPORTS A SHORT GREEN, NOT A CRASH. Beside a running lane,

## Session 107 - 2026-09-19 - an operator-directed machine stray-work sweep, and the one defect it turned up

- Shipped: CS-1154, closed. CS-1153 filed and left OPEN. Detail in `docs/LEDGER.md`, not here.

  `2026-09-19-1430-from-CS-REVIEW-e085b4a92ab2-machine-stray-work-sweep.md`; RC merges the five
  reports and the operator adjudicates before any deletion pass. NOTHING was deleted, moved or
  renamed anywhere on this box by this session.
- Decisions: no ADR. The sweep proposed a PRUNE / MOVE / KEEP / UNKNOWN class per row and
  actioned none of them; that is the operator's call after the merge.
- Surprises: THE SWEEP FOUND A LIVE DEFECT IN THE SUITE, not in the tree it was inventorying.
  `git -c core.hooksPath=.githooks push` exports its override through `GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS`,
  every git child inherits it, and a command-line override OUTRANKS repository configuration -
  so every throwaway repo in `tests/test_precommit_gate.py` lost the `core.hooksPath` it had
  just set and NO HOOK RAN. The world-name PII arm accepted the commit it exists to block,
  three pushes running, with `returncode=0` and an EMPTY stderr. The empty stderr is what
  settled it: that gate prints a PASS line on every run it completes, so silence is a hook that
  never fired, not a gate that approved. CS-1154 is the repair.
- Failed paths: the FIRST diagnosis was wrong and the ledger entry says so rather than quietly
  replacing it. The failure was attributed to a contended box - 21 python and 47 node processes
  from concurrent sibling sweeps - purely because it did not reproduce standalone. It
  reproduced three pushes running and never once outside the hook, which contention does not
  explain. Do not reach for load as an explanation before checking what the hook environment
  carries. Also measured and discarded: GIT_DIR contamination, both relative and absolute, and
  `-n auto` over `tests/test_precommit_gate.py` alone. None reproduce it.
- Process change, operator directive: the handoff is a FILE plus a Desktop shortcut, not a
  chat fence. `CS-NEXT-SESSION.txt` is tracked at the repo root, rewritten whole by every
  `/done`, rowed in `CLAUDE.md` section 4 and exempted from tier-1 budget guard (k) for the
  reason this file is. LL, LW and RC already carried that shape; CS was the one that did not.
- Next action: read `docs/item_notes/phase7.md` section CS-1153 and prune the gitignored and
  PII-bearing roots in `tools/drift_guard.py::_walk` by rule rather than by never being reached.

both hooks by a CWD-RELATIVE path. One `cd` into `moon_sync_inbox` to read notes denied
every Bash and PowerShell call in the main session AND in four dispatched subagents, which
inherit the cwd. They each lost their shell for a whole run and returned UNVERIFIABLE.
`cd <root> && <cmd>` was refused too - the hook fires before the command, so the shell
cannot recover itself. It DEFEATED the gate's own written contract, which promises exit 0
on its own error precisely so this cannot happen: that branch is unreachable when the
script is never entered. RC broadcast this exact defect, mechanism and fix to all five
trees on 2026-09-13. CS did not act on it. Seven days later it cost a day of measurement.

**CS-1162 - citation rot, and it was a recurrence against a shipped guard.** CS-1159's own
adjudicator record says "a line pointer into a living document is a citation with a shelf
life" - and a later record under the same ID did it three more times. The rule now lives in

continuation pointer following a full citation is invisible to `LINE_POINTER_RE`, 67 of them
across 8 files, 47 in two carriers whose own rules forbid editing them in place.

its own round while four trees moved, and was the LAST outstanding carrier. Vendored at
`fc22e86e...`, 25425 bytes, hashing equal. The round caught a latent defect in CS's arms,
not just its prose: CS had conflated PARTICIPANT with PIN-HOLDER, and at v1 the two counts
were equal so the wording read correctly. A sentence that is accidentally true is not a
guarded sentence.

**THE CREDENTIAL INCIDENT.** LL asked CS to look at one file in the shared git-install
scratch bucket. CS looked at the directory and found an Anthropic ADMIN-family key in
plaintext, ten days old, in a world-readable location, in CS's own litter - plus 17 world
names, the account name in 19 files, and the operator's email in two. The operator rotated;
persistence verified at MACHINE scope by hash. The render defect was HISTORICAL, closed by

repo-scoped, so nothing sees a file that is never committed; and `PLACEHOLDER_RE` can
silently neuter any rule and already has. Filed CS-1166 through CS-1169. All four siblings
answered CS's ACTION note and all four said they have no never-committed control either.

**THE REUSABLE LESSON, and it is against CS.** Three trees swept that bucket - RSC, LW,

resolves `exclude` and `per-file-ignores` against THE INVOCATION'S WORKING DIRECTORY, so a
gate that lints a temp copy can never honour a project exemption - exit 0 on the real path
and exit 1 on identical bytes in temp, same minute. The section 14 licence gate CLEARED,
with two uncomfortable facts in the register row rather than smoothed over.

## CS-1221

### Acceptance

`tests/test_hook_env_echo.py::test_no_account_name_skip_renders_the_name` passes on a
machine whose save root holds a subdirectory named in `GENERIC_SAVE_ROOT_DIRS`, and the
arm still fails when the gate really does render a planted account name - shown by the
existing control arm continuing to pass unweakened, plus a new arm that plants the generic
names while the gate's skip prose carries the colliding token and asserts the verdict
separates the two. The oracle distinguishes an occurrence the hook RENDERED from one the
hook's own fixed prose always carries; it does not do so by deleting the token from the
oracle's alphabet, by dropping `root` from `GENERIC_ACCOUNT_NAMES`, or by reading the
count down to a number that happens to pass here. If the repair edits
`tools/precommit_gate.py`, that is a frozen file and the adjudicator grant is recorded in
`docs/LEDGER.md` before the edit.

### Full headline

the account-name skip arm counts `root` inside the gate's own `save-root` prose, so a correct gate reads as a leak

### MEASURED 2026-10-02, the pre-push suite blocked this session's push (session 118)

The pre-push hook refused at an unpublished CS-1214 commit with one failure and nothing pushed - the notice
reported exit 0, which is the shape `memory/` already records. `1 failed, 6537 passed in
359.61s`, the failure being
`test_no_account_name_skip_renders_the_name[generic-account-names]`: an account name
occurred 1 time in the hook output where the arm requires 0.

A probe that re-ran the arm's own driver and printed the matching LINE located it exactly.
The arm plants `USERNAME=admin` and `USER=root`, both members of the gate's
`GENERIC_ACCOUNT_NAMES`, and then forbids either token in the hook output. The single hit
is the gate's own skip-reason prose, emitted from `tools/precommit_gate.py` where the
save-root branch prefixes `_matchable`'s reason: the compound `save-root` carries `root` as
a bounded token, because `bounded_hits` guards its match with `(?<![A-Za-z0-9])` and a
hyphen is not an alphanumeric. So a gate that correctly REFUSED to match on a generic name
is read as having leaked one.

The defect is in the oracle, not the gate: the arm cannot tell a token the hook rendered
from a token the hook's fixed prose always carries. NONE of this session's four changed
files is involved - the diff against `3cc7175` touches `.github/workflows/tier1.yml`,
`ROADMAP.md`, `docs/item_notes/phase7.md` and `tests/test_tier1_budget.py` only.

WHY IT FIRED NOW, AND WHY CI DOES NOT SEE IT. That skip line is printed only when the save
root holds a subdirectory whose name is in `GENERIC_SAVE_ROOT_DIRS`, so the arm's verdict
depends on the operator's live save library rather than on the tree. A CI runner has no
save directory at all and takes a different branch, which is why tier 1 stayed green while
every local push is refused. The arm is therefore machine-dependent in a way its name does
not say.

### RECORDED 2026-10-02, the adjudicator's ruling and the repair it took (session 118)

THE RULING, which is not re-litigated here. A BASELINE-DIFFERENCED ORACLE wins: run the
same commit twice - once with the arm's own names planted, once with names the same branch
drops that share no token with them - and refuse only the EXCESS over what the baseline
found. Prose the hook always carries appears in both runs and cancels; a real rendering
appears in one and reddens.

REWORDING THE GATE'S SKIP PROSE WAS REFUSED, AND SO WAS THE FROZEN-FILE GRANT FOR IT.
`tools/precommit_gate.py` stayed byte-identical through this repair. The reason is the
dependency direction: the gate behaved correctly - it REFUSED to match on a generic name
and said so - and the fault was the oracle's inability to tell a carried token from a
rendered one. Editing a correct frozen gate to satisfy a defective test inverts that
dependency and buys a green arm with a worse tree. Also refused as acceptance-forbidden:
narrowing `bounded_hits`, a hyphen exception, any compound-aware token rule, dropping
`root` or `admin` from a generic list, and reading the bound down to a number that
happens to pass here.

WHAT THE REPAIR IS, in `tests/test_hook_env_echo.py` alone. `account_skip_run` measures
one commit and takes what it COUNTS as a parameter separate from what it PLANTS, so a
baseline run plants values that cannot add to the count. `account_skip_verdict` runs both
and returns a `SkipVerdict` of scalars - the excess is `rendered`. Both runs reach the
same branch, which the arm asserts of each, so every line of fixed prose between them is
identical by construction rather than by inspection. The baselines are the short pair
`wv`/`kp` and the generic pair `guest`/`owner`.

THE NEW ARM, machine-independent where the defect was not.
`test_the_skip_arm_separates_a_carried_token_from_a_rendered_one` plants the colliding
carriage into a SANDBOX gate copy - the tracked gate is never written - sets the planted
account name TO the carried token, and asserts the token IS present before asserting the
verdict separates it. One case per prose shape measured in the gate: the save-root
subdirectory skip and the save-root entry cap, both carrying `root`, and the two
absolute-home-path findings, both carrying `home`.

THAT IS FOUR PROSE SHAPES OVER TWO TOKEN CLASSES, NOT FOUR BRANCHES, and the first wording
of this paragraph said "one case per site" as though it were the latter. An independent
refutation pass measured what the cases actually enter: all four plant into the SINGLE
generic skip line and reach the generic branch. They are not vacuous - `shown` is at or
above the carried count and `carried` is at least 2 in each, so the carriage demonstrably
renders - but they model the three unreachable sites rather than covering them, and the
distinction is the whole difference between a measurement and a model.

ALL FOUR SIBLING CARRIAGES CANCEL, measured this session with the baselines live:
`shown` equals `carried` and `rendered` is 0 for every one of them, and for the live
save-root line the main arm's own numbers are 1 and 1. The save-root cases read one count
higher than the planted carriage alone, which is that live line being counted as well -
it cancels too. Stated as unverified rather than claimed: the entry-cap line and the two
home-path findings are not REACHABLE on this machine, so their cancellation is proven on
the planted model of each, not against a live emission.

NON-VACUITY, PROVEN BY PLANTING A REAL LEAK. A gate copy whose generic skip line renders
the VALUE alongside the key - so the branch is still reached - makes the repaired arm red
with an excess of 2. The pre-existing control
`test_a_gate_copy_whose_skip_renders_the_name_is_caught` is untouched by the diff, gets no
baseline, and still passes on both of its plants.

## CS-1219

### Acceptance

a tracked witness records the candidate an adjudication was dispatched over and refuses a
verdict taken over a tree that moved under it: the witness records the candidate's tree
object rather than its commit, so a commit that leaves the tree identical is not a move
and an uncommitted edit is, and it covers compiled bytecode as well as tracked files,
because `__pycache__/` is gitignored and a porcelain check is blind to a swapped `.pyc`.
Shown by two arms, red first: one that edits a tracked file under a recorded freeze and
asserts the witness reddens, and one that leaves every tracked file byte-identical while
swapping a reachable `.pyc` and asserts the witness reddens for that reason alone. The
prose in `tools/headless-queue.md` and `CLAUDE.md` section 5 then points at the witness
rather than carrying the rule alone, and neither file restates what the witness measures.

### Full headline

the adjudication candidate freeze is prose with no mechanical witness, and a porcelain one would be blind to a swapped `.pyc`

### FILED 2026-10-02, an inbox-derived finding that survived refutation (session 118)

`tools/headless-queue.md`, under its "Freeze the candidate before dispatching an
adjudicator" bullet, and `CLAUDE.md` section 5 both order the candidate frozen
before dispatch. A sweep of `tools/`, `tests/`, `ops/` and `.githooks/` for the rule found
only prose: every `freeze`-shaped hit is a `frozenset`, a `drift_guard` frozen-files
report, or the doctrine itself. Nothing records an adjudication's subject and nothing
re-checks it at verdict time. The harm is already MEASURED rather than hypothetical -
`CLAUDE.md` section 5 records that the tree moved under an adjudicator four times in
session 45 and that three whole-suite runs were spent proving a run straddling an edit
says nothing. The bytecode half is live too: `.gitignore` excludes `__pycache__/`, so a
porcelain-based witness reports a clean tree while a stale or swapped `.pyc` sits on disk
and is what the interpreter loads.

## CS-1222

### Acceptance

a doc carrying an unresolvable commit sha turns a guard red: a tracked gate resolves
every sha-shaped citation in the authored docs with `git rev-parse --verify -q
<sha>^{commit}` and FAILS on one that does not resolve, red first, with an arm that
plants an unresolvable sha in a temp copy of a guarded doc and asserts the refusal, and
a second arm that plants a RESOLVABLE one and asserts it passes so the gate is not
merely refusing every hex run. The gate's inclusion rule is published and its exclusion
set is reported per run, because a sweep that admits nothing reports clean; the known
non-commit classes measured on 2026-10-02 - agent and worktree ids, sha256 prefixes,
foreign-repository licence pins, git blob sha1s, lane run ids and synthetic fixture
vectors - are each excluded by a STATED rule rather than by a path exemption. An empty
result is never reported as a pass on its own: the gate states whether SS's
discriminator was available, since `.git/filter-repo/` is absent here and a check that
cannot fire proves nothing.

### Full headline

`docs/LEDGER.md` forbids citing a commit sha and nothing enforces it, so a doc carrying an unresolvable sha reddens nothing

### MEASURED 2026-10-02, found answering the channel's re-pin round (session 118)

`docs/LEDGER.md` already forbids the citation: "Cite the item ID, the merged file, and
the test name. Do not cite the slice SHA.", and its invalid-pointer list names "A bare
commit SHA" outright. NOTHING ENFORCES IT. Four tools validate a commit field's SHAPE
with a regex and never call git - the measurement record's `_COMMIT` pattern over
`tools/measurements.json`, and the concentration, growth and headroom tools;
`tests/test_docs_citations.py` grades symbol-shaped pointers and is silent on shas; the
one site that resolves a ref resolves a flip ref rather than a doc citation.

THE SWEEP THAT FOUND IT CAME BACK CLEAN, WHICH IS THE POINT. 59 files, 765 sha-shaped
occurrences, 393 distinct, 353 resolving as commits and 40 empty - and all 40 are
explained by their own citing lines as things that were never commits. So CS's record is
clean by discipline and not by any gate, and the next unresolvable sha to land will land
silently. A clean result standing in for a guard is the shape
`memory/` already records under a gate that skips its checks reporting PASS.

taken in.
